He later spoke Spanish with a physio at Newcastle as he targeted a move to Barcelona, while the winger also underwent six formal lessons.

Joao Gomes is among Wolves' foreign imports to have worked with a specialist language tech giant to help them settle at the club.

Arsenal put a bonus in Emiliano Martinez's contract to encourage him to learn English.

Trent Alexander-Arnold worked with a Spanish tutor for five months before his move to Real Madrid.

Glasner had maintained that his squad will have to work hard and show commitment both on and off the pitch to improve.

'The most vital thing is that players want to improve, then it can happen.'.

Glasner met with Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis in London earlier this week, where plans for the January transfer window were discussed.

Industry observers note that 'We need to improve in the squad, in the staff, in the environment and this is our discussion. It was a fantastic meeting and it was worth spending six hours travelling.'.

Forest face a Chelsea side on Friday that have lost three of their last four league matches.

  • Jagiellonia Bialystok goalkeeper Slawomir Abramowicz has revealed that his dream transfer would be to Liverpool.
  • On Thursday night, Abramowicz was between the sticks to help the Polish side earn a 1-1 draw at Sunderland in the Europa League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 17:30.

Jagiellonia Bialystok goalkeeper Slawomir Abramowicz has revealed that his dream transfer would be to Liverpool.

On Thursday night, Abramowicz was between the sticks to help the Polish side earn a 1-1 draw at Sunderland in the Europa League.

Helping his side to a share of the spoils versus a Premier League club was the latest achievement for the 22-year-old, who has recently made his debut for Poland.

While he holds a contract at Jagiellonia until 2028, Abramowicz is naturally being linked with a number of higher-profile clubs.

The likes of Fulham and Ipswich Town have recently been credited as admirers of the goalkeeper.

Nevertheless, Abramowicz has suggested that he has his sights set on a future move to Anfield.

According to recent reports, in comments relayed by Transfery Info, he noted: "My dream league is England, I think. In my opinion, this is a temple of football.".

When pushed on his preferred club, he added: "Of course, I would play a whole season there. That's my ultimate dream.

"Favourite Premier League club? Liverpool.".

As someone who has conceded just 153 goals in 127 matches for Jagiellonia, Abramowicz is definitely progressing in the right direction.

With Alisson Becker having just turned 34 years of age, Liverpool may also be considering long-term successors for the Brazilian.

However, the assumption is that Abramowicz will need to prove himself at another club before being viewed as a genuine option by a club of Liverpool's size.

Liverpool have also invested heavily in Giorgi Mamardashvili, who has a contract at the Merseyside giants until 2031.

#164729. Tech Report: Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Two points dropped in a game of two halves

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1407 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Arseblog ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Two points dropped in a game of two halves

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1407 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment.
  • In a recent development, A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time.
  • The lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment. Arsenal were 1-0 up, well on top and absolutely deserving of the lead. Newcastle had struggled to exert any kind of control, and we’d already had 9 attempts on goal.

In a recent development, A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time. Unfortunately for him and for us, Lewis Hall produced a quite outstanding piece of defending to slide in and block the shot over the bar. That was the difference between Arsenal going in 2-0 up at the break rather than with just the single goal margin.

The lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back. Newcastle’s only chance had come early, a shot from Jacob Murphy that deflected off his own player and drifted wide with David Raya wrong-footed. After that, we bossed the half, with 11 shots in total, 65% possession, but still only that one goal.

According to recent reports, it feels redundant to say this is a very, very good Arsenal team, but if we have a weakness, it’s that we don’t turn this kind of domination into more goals. Very often we don’t need to as our defensive solidity and consistency keeps the opposition at bay, but last night we let our standards slip in that regard, and the lack of firepower or being clinical in the final third came home to roost.

Industry observers note that it was, very literally, a game of two halves. Newcastle made a triple sub at the break and it would be churlish not to give them credit for the fact it made a positive impact. However, the Arsenal performance was night and day. The opposition upped the energy and intensity, and we made mistakes. Odegaard miskicking a Riccardo Calafiori throw-in provided them the opportunity to equalise, and I do wonder why Harvey Barnes was so free at the back post to slide home for 1-1.

That goal gave them momentum, they caused us problems again and again, some of them of our own making with carelessness and misfortune. Eze got back well to defend in our box but unfortunately slipped, Raya’s clearance was unconvincing and then Gabriel had to boot the ball behind for a corner – from which they made it 2-1. Dan Burn drifted off Jurrien Timber to get a free header, the ball scrambled around a bit before Malick Thiaw poked it over the line to give them the lead. Messy, shambolic defending – not very Arsenal at all.

Industry observers note that if we’re being fair, we have to say they could have scored again. David Raya went off with a shoulder injury, Kepa had to make a smart save at the feet of Lewis Miley but why was he one on one with the keeper in the first place? A Joe Willock shot deflected wide in similar fashion to the Murphy one in the first half, and eventually Arteta changed things with Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly coming on for Eze and Bruno Guimaraes who had a quiet return to his former club – bar that first half moment when he almost got enough contact on a fantastic Declan Rice cross but could only put the ball wide from close range.

Recent findings suggest that we did get an equaliser, and very well worked it was too. We played the ball across the back line from right to left, into midfield where Havertz’s smart dummy allowed Odegaard room to drive on and find Madueke. He was Arsenal’s best attacking player last night, he kept trying to make things happen, and while I think the Newcastle keeper will probably have nightmares about letting that shot in, Madueke deserved the goal, and it earned us a point.

It has been revealed that it was after the 90th minute when the manager brought on Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino to try and find a winner, the Swede had one shot over the bar from the edge of the box, but had we found another, it would have been a real smash and grab. In the end, the draw was probably a fair result based on how the game played out, and afterwards the manager was unhappy at leaving two points behind:.

My feeling is that we have lost two points today. And I say we because we were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. It should have been two, three or four-nil up, clear. But it wasn’t.

Industry observers note that we started to lose duels, we started to lose second balls. We gave the ball away and have really poor circulation balls against their press and their waves. And when that happens, you give them belief.

It’s a pity because the margin should have been, again, much bigger for the level that we’ve shown.

Recent findings suggest that and this is the key for me. It should have been, but it wasn’t, and it too often isn’t. As I mentioned above, our defensive brilliance is fundamental to us winning so many games, but football is a game of variance. You can’t always control everything. On another night Odegaard just puts his foot through that throw in and that first Newcastle goal doesn’t happen. Eze and Raya deal better with that situation and we don’t concede a corner. We can focus on those individual things and say we could and should do better for sure, but you have to allow for some of that over the course of a season. You cannot be perfect for 90+ minutes 38 games in every league campaign.

The ongoing issue for me is our firepower though. I thought generally the front three played pretty well last night, and it’s not as if we missed a glut of chances, but it’s about turning the level of dominance we had in that first half into more goals. This isn’t a one-time issue either. We scored two lovely goals last night but we should have had that game firmly in our grasp at half-time, but in this league a single goal margin is never a sure thing.

Industry observers note that the summer was a let-down in an attacking sense, there’s no getting away from that. If we had a forward line that was even close to our midfield and defence in terms of quality and depth, the Premier League would be a cakewalk. I know that’s a bit simplistic, but it’s also a fact. Regardless of what you think of the business, we let goals go to Turkey and Saudi Arabia, and replaced them with a player who has yet to score. Which isn’t to lay the blame at the feet of Tzolis, far from it, but with the squad planning/building that was undertaken.

For me, January becomes increasingly notable because the improvement required is obvious, and for a sporting director whose track record looks quite hit and miss as it is, he needs a convincing window or the questions around the job he’s doing will become louder and louder, and for good reason.

It has been revealed that the other big issue from yesterday was the injury to David Raya. It didn’t look good at all, and any absence for him would be a huge blow to the team. He’s been the best in the Premier League, and perhaps the best in Europe, for the last 18 months, and inevitably there’s a drop-off when any club is without their first choice keeper for any period of time. That’s another adjustment we’re probably going to have to make, and if it means we’re likely to be less secure and clean sheets are harder to come by, then that issue of scoring goals and being more potent comes into even sharper focus. Let’s keep fingers crossed it’s not as bad as it appears to be.

Industry observers note that right, I’ll leave it there for now. There’s plenty to unpick from this one, so I’ll leave you to it in the Arses. More here tomorrow, including an Arsecast Extra. Until then, have a great Sunday.

#164728. Mind the gap

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (892 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arseblog ↗ Open Full Page

Mind the gap

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that over the last few weeks, I’ve grown accustomed to waking up and experiencing low-level fear first thing in the morning.
  • With any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them.
  • If Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that over the last few weeks, I’ve grown accustomed to waking up and experiencing low-level fear first thing in the morning. Today, it was a nice change not to be focused on my own health, and instead for my anxiety to centre around someone else – David Raya.

With any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them. It doesn’t mean there isn’t still a kind of hierarchy, just that you’re better able to cope if injury or suspension hits. Mikel Arteta referencing ‘finishers’ rather than substitutes might be a psychological ploy to keep his squad happy, but it’s more easy to apply when you have the group of players he has at his disposal.

If Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White. If Riccardo Calafiori can’t play, Piero Hincapie can. We all worried about William Saliba needing a long lay-off after the World Cup, but the arrival of Ezri Konsa offset that in exemplary fashion. If we miss Declan Rice, we have two World Cup winners, a Brazilian international, and one of the most highly regarded young English midfielders around to fill that gap. Further forward, Noni Madueke is performing at a level that makes Bukayo Saka’s absence feel less impactful than it would have previously, and while I think forward line quality remains an issue we need to solve as urgently as January, you can flip a coin between most of our options there without feeling you’ve weakened yourself considerably.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, I don’t think the same applies between the sticks. Raya has been the stand-out goalkeeper of the last few years, establishing himself as Arsenal’s number 1 after an initial settling in period. One, by the way, which I don’t think the manager handled particularly well. Typically he’s been near flawless in terms of his man-management, and while he was fundamentally right about wanting the Spaniard to come in and take the position to a new level, the way he fudged things around Aaron Ramsdale, talking about how he’d sub a goalkeeper in a game and all that nonsense really wasn’t his best moment. It left both of his keepers in a weird place for too long, until Raya’s confidence grew and his quality came to the fore.

Since then he’s won multiple golden glove awards, his shot-stopping has been incredible at times, and although every player and every keeper will make mistakes, his have been few and far between. For me though, despite the eye-catching acrobatics – which are more easily clipped up for the social media generation – his key asset is the assurance he brings to the team. Not just when he has the ball at his feet (even if there are times I would like him to move it more swiftly), but how good he is from opposition set-pieces and crosses. He comes and claims and eases pressure time and time again, and I think that’s the thing we’re going to miss most if he’s out for any significant period of time.

In a recent development, kepa is obviously a very experienced second choice, but is second choice for a reason. Realistically though, I don’t think there’s much any club can do to have a back-up option that’s nearly as good as their number 1. If you’re being brutally honest, many clubs in the Premier League don’t have a first choice that comes anywhere close to be as good as Raya, despite their best efforts and spending millions to try and find that player. So, as anxious as I am about him being out, it is one of those things we can’t really complain about. We just have to get on with it.

As I mentioned in yesterday’s blog, we are probably going to be less secure at the back, that feels kind of inevitable, so the onus on the players further forward increases. Score more goals, turn that domination of possession and territory into more chances. If we have the ball in their half, our goalkeeper becomes something of a non-glitch for as long as that’s the case. There are ways to cope, but we might need to gird our loins for some iffy moments at the back that we haven’t had to experience too often of late.

Sources indicate that as Arsenal fans though, we’ve come through worse than this with goalkeepers in the past. I don’t want to give anyone PTSD first thing on a Monday morning, but when you’ve lived what we’ve lived in seasons gone by, hopefully a little Kepa period won’t be too traumatic. And maybe, after the scan, there’ll be better news about Raya than we expect. Fingers crossed.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

Recent findings suggest that pod should be out around noon. Until then!

Welcome to another Arsecast Extra, the Arsenal podcast, with myself and James from @gunnerblog.

In this Interlull episode we look back on Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle at St James’ Park. We chat about an impressive first half from Arsenal, taking a deserved lead into the break through Eberechi Eze’s fine goal, but should that dominance and control have brought a bigger lead? We then try to figure out how and why things went so wrong in the second half, falling behind as Newcastle scored twice due to our own carelessness, before Noni Madueke capped a good performance with a very well worked equaliser. Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (843 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.
  • According to recent reports, "Faith does not justify exclusion.
  • According to recent reports, "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related concerns and the athletic performance of individual players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

According to recent reports, "Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was debuted.

According to recent reports, "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related concerns and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.".

The fan club states their problem is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club said "gives us cause to reassess the situation.".

This campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (MAJOR) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:.

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold.".

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

The fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends.".

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's plan" and that homosexuality is a sin.

According to recent reports, borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone.".

Article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

The use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Massive-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit.".

And yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the latest opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery, Damian Vidagany deliver contradictory Alejandro Garnacho messages

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 17:31.
  • Unai Emery and Damian Vidagany have seemingly contradicted each other with regards to Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa future.
  • Having been omitted from three Villa squads in a row, the Chelsea loanee has been a hot topic for debate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 17:31.

Unai Emery and Damian Vidagany have seemingly contradicted each other with regards to Alejandro Garnacho's Aston Villa future.

Having been omitted from three Villa squads in a row, the Chelsea loanee has been a hot topic for debate.

After Emery swiftly decided against activating a £35m option to sign Liverpool's Harvey Elliott in 2025-26, Garnacho being frozen out after seven substitute appearances when a £43m permanent transfer could become an obligation if a certain amount of matches are played appears to be close to an identical situation.

At a press conference on Friday, Emery insisted that he 'respected' Garnacho but was choosing to select other players.

Emery also claimed that "the club is running" matters during the winter transfer window. However, Vidagany told a club forum on Thursday that Emery was in full control.

Vidagany - the club's head of football operations - claims that Villa chiefs "follow Unai Emery" and that the Spaniard has "full power" over transfers.

He said: "I know that is a topic that everyone wants to know. You can give me 3,000 lbs of pressure, but there is only one fact. In Aston Villa, the sporting decisions are taken by Unai Emery.

Sources indicate that "Emery decides if a player will or will not be in the squad according to the criteria of Unai Emery. Emery is picking other players and decided not to put him in the squad.

"This can change or not, I don't know. It will depend maybe on the performance of the player. We are a club who tries to be efficient with the resources we have.

"There is no question that Emery has full power on who is in the squad and who is not. Any noise outside of us, it is something that we don't want to control or discuss.

According to recent reports, "We follow Unai Emery, he is our leader. He knows deeper than anyone what the squad needs.".

When Aston Villa loaned Garnacho from Chelsea, it was widely claimed that it would be easier to activate the set amount of appearances required for a permanent transfer to proceed than with Elliott.

Elliott needed to make 10 appearances. With Garnacho having made seven substitute outings before being frozen out, the assumption is that eight or nine matches is the so-called magic number.

Recent findings suggest that villa have no loan break option that they can enforce, nor do Chelsea have a recall clause. Therefore, if the clubs cannot reach a fresh agreement over financial terms, Garnacho faces the realistic prospect of not playing again in 2026-27.

Garnacho is, theoretically, available for selection for seven more matches to be played this year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that arsenal are in Champions League action this evening, taking on Borussia Dortmund at home. It’s a game that Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in the absence of David Raya, but the news around the Arsenal number 1 was a little more positive than expected. In his press conference yesterday, Mikel Arteta said:.

He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected.

Industry observers note that we expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at that moment, and the first test that we’ve done demonstrated something that is much more encouraging. There’s no need for surgery, which was the main fear especially because that would rule him out for months, so let’s see.

So, it seems like he’s going to miss a few games, but not anything prolonged, which is obviously good news. Elsewhere, there’s room for rotation, and I think this might be a good chance to give minutes to William Saliba who hasn’t played competitively since the World Cup. He’s had a couple of behind closed doors appearances, which will be useful in terms of fitness, but nothing compares with actually playing at this level.

I wonder too if players like Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie will fancy their chances, but that seems like a lot of change in the back four – and the goalkeeper – so we’ll have to wait and see there. In midfield, we can bring Myles Lewis-Skelly in for a start, but obviously the manager has plenty to choose from in there, and up front I imagine it will be a chance for Viktor Gyokeres whose minutes have been scant so far this season. Asked if the striker had been knocking on his door about that, Arteta noted:.

No, we have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing, to gather information about the way they are feeling, and so far, it’s been very positive with Viktor and with the rest of the team.

He could really use a goal tonight if he does start, as does Christos Tzolis whose numbers so far this season aren’t where you’d like them to be. Obviously there’s more to assessing a player than simply goals and assists, but for a left winger brought into replace two players who contributed a lot to the team over the last few seasons, just two assists from 11 appearances (Community Shield excluded) is a little below what you’d hope. He has had an injury, of course, but if his season needs a kick-start, tonight would be very timely.

Dortmund sit top of the Bundesliga right now, unbeaten in the league thus far, and with just one defeat all season in all competitions. That did come in the Champions League, away to Bodo Glimt, but this will be a tricky test tonight for Arsenal. Arteta says:.

It has been revealed that I’m very impressed with them, you see the results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga at the top and where they are in the Champions League and especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat they are able to create. We had them here in pre-season, and they highlighted the quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that. But we play at home in front of our crowd, and now we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

According to recent reports, after a disappointing second half against Newcastle on Saturday, I’m sure the manager will be looking for a response from his side. It’s nice to be at home again, and a long spell of games in London will hopefully less taxing physically without all the travel, so it’d be good to get that off to a winning start tonight.

Elsewhere, Bruno Guimaraes spoke about his first few months at the club, and how he now feels like he’s getting to grips with what Mikel Arteta wants from him, saying:.

Recent findings suggest that I’m here, I don’t know, three, four months? It’s still a lot to go, but I now definitely understand my role in the team, the way that Mikel wants me to play in the team. So, yeah, I think I still can play much, much better.

And it’s quite interesting to hear him talk about how at Arsenal he is more ‘free’ than he was under Eddie Howe at Newcastle. Most would feel it was the other way around, but he explained:.

In a recent development, it’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

According to recent reports, if you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.

In a recent development, I think there’s more to come from him, he’s looked good at times, a little off the pace at others, and I think my main worry is about the physical side of his game. Does he have the running power and athleticism that enables players like Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to thrive under this manager? At 29, he’s no spring chicken, but I guess there’s always room for improvement. Anyway, his press conference stuff from yesterday is worth reading, and there’s some good chat about him on the Arsecast Extra which you’ll find below.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. 📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1737 w)

Tech Report: Arsenal 1-1 Dortmund: Familiar flaws hold Arsenal back

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.
  • Recent findings suggest that arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert massive chances when the time comes.
  • I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert massive chances when the time comes. And the way the team is starting games after the break is worrying, with teams who are battered to within an inch of their lives early on suddenly able to compete.

I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog. One where I’m miserable, of course: the players can’t shoot, they make all the wrong choices in the decisive moment, we can’t keep wasting chances and dropping off after the break, if Andrea Berta doesn’t deliver the true heirs to Thierry Henry and Robert Pires in January, then he should be stuffed into one of the cannons outside the Armoury and fired into the cold night air.

The other version is much more glass half full: Arteta is coaching masterclasses every week, this level of dominance in games is something I could only dream of a few years ago, that’s the most shots we’ve had in a game all season, we’re top of the league, we’re creating loads without any set-piece reliance and without Bukayo Saka – the goals will come.

It has been revealed that some people reading this would prefer (and relate better to) one version, and others the other version, I’m sure. Let’s see where we end up!

In a recent development, there were, as there tends to be in these Champions League games, a fair few changes from the weekend. Kepa, Piero Hincapie, Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis, and Viktor Gyokeres all came into the team.

Recent findings suggest that despite featuring half a different side, there were plenty of parallels with the Newcastle match. Arsenal were dominant from the off, with Hincapie and White taking turns to play off of Gyokeres. Dortmund had no idea how to cover them and both fullbacks were the targets of early crosses into the box.

After a couple of long-range efforts, Arsenal got their goal they deserved, with Gyokeres launching a ferocious, dipping effort beyond Gregor Kobel. The Swede can put his foot through the ball, that’s for sure, and the Dortmund backline gave him the sort of time and space to set himself that he doesn’t often get.

The pressure continued after the opener for a while, with Tzolis forcing a good save and Madueke just unable to sort his feet to tap in the rebound.

It’s fair to say the game settled down after 15/20 minutes, with Dortmund growing into it a little, but it was still Arsenal who looked like scoring the next goal. Rice shot over from almost the same patch of grass Gyokeres had scored from, and the midfielder had another chance when a beautiful one-touch move ended with him bursting through, hurtling towards the Dortmund box. Maybe he could’ve picked out Madueke in support, but he went alone and Nico Schlotterbeck just got across to block the shot.

Industry observers note that another huge chance was denied by the offside flag as much as the finishing – Madueke won the ball high, Odegaard squared it to Gyokeres, and the Swede fired over from near the penalty spot. Odegaard was ruled offside but I’m not convinced: had the ball hit the net, I think we’d have seen a very tight VAR check.

There was one thought on everyone’s minds at half-time: don’t do the same thing again. After Slavia Prague and Newcastle, do not do the same thing again.

Arsenal did the same thing again.

According to recent reports, gyokeres was, by UEFA standards, lucky not to concede a penalty when a corner struck him on the arm. There was another early warning sign with Dortmund sliding the ball across the box and Maximilian Beier kicking the air. He didn’t make the same mistake with his next opportunity. Centre-back Joane Gadou (who was very impressive all evening) charged through the heart of the pitch before playing the ball to Beier, who jinked to unbalance Gabriel and slotted home.

In a recent development, sometimes a goal is just a good goal, and I don’t think anyone was really at fault here. It’s a great run from Gadou, Beier tricks Gabriel to take the ball onto his weaker left side – it’s fair if Gabriel is expecting (and blocking the angle) on the attacker’s favoured foot, I know how that can happen. I think if we score that goal we’re talking about two brilliant individuals, rather than defensive errors.

According to recent reports, my first thought? Not again. My second? OK, how do we respond? Because on Saturday, the response was poor.

This time it was a lot better. Jobe Bellingham had a rebound disallowed for offside, a moment that really brought the crowd back into the game, but in truth, that was Dortmund’s only real moment of threat. From the goal on 55 minutes to full-time, Arsenal had 15 shots to Dortmund’s two.

And that doesn’t include Serhou Guirassy playing one-twos with the post after a clever, low free-kick from Martin Odegaard late on.

Madueke had an effort blocked. Gyokeres flicked a header wide. Madueke shot wide beyond the far post after a good run. Gyokeres missed a substantial chance with his head from six yards out. Rice hit the near post from a tight angle after a brilliant pass from Eberechi Eze.

A couple of late corners came to nothing, and that was it.

Mikel Arteta was clearly pleased with the performance on the whole:.

Well, I think I love the way the team played. There’s no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game … It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn’t ended up in the back of the net. That’s my feeling.

to do what we’ve done out there is just something to be very, very pleased about, because there is very little more that we can demand from the team.

But we all know what that little more is:.

According to recent reports, obviously the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, the amount of chances, the situation, and even shots that are not there. We are three against two, two against one, and the ball doesn’t land with the right person. There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.

In a recent development, often when Arsenal don’t win games, it feels like it’s because the team haven’t created enough chances. We end up focusing on that one moment, where that one player didn’t execute the way you wanted. But last night wasn’t one of those: Arsenal didn’t struggle to turn dominance into good, slick football, and that football into a healthy number of decent opportunities.

In a recent development, that’s incredibly frustrating, but I do think you win a lot more often than not when you do that. Maybe that’s a hard sell for some this morning, but it’s how I feel about it when we play well, especially when we’ve been winning games anyway. That’s the first time this season we’ve gone two without a win across all competitions, and we’ve won 14 of 19 games so far. Sometimes things don’t fall for you, and this one felt a lot like ‘one of those’, certainly more than Newcastle did.

A word for a couple of promising performances too, with the boss asked about Gyokeres in his post-match press conference:.

According to recent reports, what I love the most is how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threw it in behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the victory that we need.

In a recent development, his finishing was off after the brilliant opener, but at least he was in the positions: too often this season and last, Gyokeres has gone through a game barely registering a shot. He had seven last night, and if he can do that more often he’ll score a lot more. His general play was improved too, both holding the ball up and competing in behind.

According to recent reports, and I thought Martin Odegaard was excellent too. His eight chances created from open play was the most of any player in any Champions League match so far this season.

Recent findings suggest that since we returned to the competition in 2023, we’ve had a player create more than five chances in a match just twice: Odegaard at Napoli in September (6) and Odegaard last night (9). He’s incredibly unlucky not to be leaving the game with a couple of assists.

The draw leaves us in a decent position to finish in the all-key top eight in the league phase still, although you have to squint a bit to see us landing in the also-important top two. Real Madrid are up next and that’s a reminder of the sort of teams we’re up against: finishing in the top two is a tall order at the best of times.

With each passing game, it is impossible not to wonder what could be done in January to add to the team. Unless there’s a sudden uptick out of nowhere, those thoughts aren’t disappearing. And even if there is a massive uptick, those thoughts will still be around. But 30 shots is the most we’ve had in a game all season, and the same group of players have scored more goals with fewer shots (/chances) plenty of times. Let’s hope we see some more clinical finishing on Sunday.

Guess I landed on the glass half full version.

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

This young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

Ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. Out to get warm! ♨️ https://t.co/75qTJA6L42.

Recent findings suggest that we have two crucial wins for us but we cannot stop. A very good team in front of us and I hope we are at the level of the game.

According to recent reports, different circumstances. It’s out fourth game in 10 days, Florian [Wirtz] and Bradley [Barcola] have played almost every minute so we have to be sensible and the same with Alex [Isak].

I think he is doing very well [Leiws Koumas], or else we would not trust him to start these kinds of games.

Villarreal XI: Gulacsi, Mourino, Navarro, Veiga, Cardona, Saliba, Gueye, Buchanan, Comesana, Moleiro, Mikautadze.

Subs: Junior, Costa, Freeman, Diatta, Gerard, Foyth, Akhomach, Macia, Oluwaseyi, Perez, El Jmili, Gaitan Diaz.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Gravenberch, Nyoni, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Koumas, Gakpo.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Kerkez, Wirtz, Isak, Barcola, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Laffey.

It has been revealed that A very interesting team selection from Andoni Iraola. Liverpool’s head coach had indicated at his pre-match press conference that he was going to go as strong as possible, as his side seek to secure their third straight Champions League win. But the very fact Iraola has chosen to put Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola on the bench indicates he has one eye on Sunday’s demanding assignment against Brighton at Anfield.

Iraola will be delighted to have Cody Gakpo fit again and Lewis Koumas certainly deserves another opportunity to lead the line. But after victory’s against Atletico Madrid and LASK, Liverpool have given themselves some breathing space and it is understandable if Iraola, who has bemoaned the lack of time he has to train his squad, is already plotting Brighton’s downfall.

Your Reds to take on Villarreal in the #UCL! 🔴💫 https://t.co/tlQNFZVMBv.

In a recent development, the club known as the “Yellow Submarine” made themselves some fans in the red half of Merseyside by denying Everton a place in the Champions League proper in 2005/06. Everton lost 4-2 on aggregate, and there was controversy in the second leg in Spain when Pierluigi Collina disallowed a Duncan Ferguson header that could have taken the tie to extra time. Everton had finished fourth, one place above Liverpool, the previous season, but Liverpool’s triumph in Istanbul assured them of a qualification place too. Unlike Everton, they prevailed.

Speaking of which, Rafael Benitez is at Anfield this evening.

Sources indicate that dominic King takes stock of Andoni Iraola’s first 10 games in charge of Liverpool and, despite some teething problems, he believes there are reasons to be optimistic. The demands Iraola is putting on Liverpool’s midfielders are an interesting tactical wrinkle, with Dom writing: “Liverpool’s formation will always be written as 4-2-3-1, but the reality is that Iraola’s team do not play in four clear tactical lines. He asks specific jobs of his midfielders, deploying them detailed instructions, and it is going to require some patience before performances become consistent.”.

A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

Liverpool drew Atletico Madrid at home (already ticked off) and Inter Milan away as their two pot-one fixtures, which is about as kind as you can expect. A top-two finish in the league phase is a realistic aspiration for Andoni Iraola’s team, and something would need to go badly awry for them to miss out on the top eight.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

They have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

Iraola will be up against his close friend and former Athletic Bilbao team-mate Inigo Perez who is now in charge at Villarreal. Perez was also Iraola’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano, the job which earned the Basque his move to Bournemouth. Perez guided Rayo Vallecano to the Uefa Conference League final last season.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that thanks to Lewis for taking care of the blog yesterday as I was unable to watch the Borussia Dortmund match live.
  • In a recent development, I think while I have some frustrations overall with our inability to turn dominance into goals, I’m more comfortable with it when we’re actually making chances.
  • It wasn’t that long ago that it was the other way around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that thanks to Lewis for taking care of the blog yesterday as I was unable to watch the Borussia Dortmund match live. I saw that we’d scored early but only saw the final score well after the full-time whistle, so I guess it was a little disappointing not to have built on that fantastic hit from Viktor Gyokeres.

In a recent development, I think while I have some frustrations overall with our inability to turn dominance into goals, I’m more comfortable with it when we’re actually making chances. I think the manager would have a far bigger issue on his hands if we weren’t, and on Tuesday night the fact we had 30 attempts on goal tells you the problem isn’t chance creation, it’s about being clinical.

It wasn’t that long ago that it was the other way around. We found it hard to make goalscoring opportunities and for me that’s much more of a worry. It doesn’t mean we can’t improve, it doesn’t mean January becomes any less important the closer it gets, it’s just that the solution lies with the players we have who should be capable of better. There were a couple of other opportunities for Gyokeres that could easily have made this a better night for him and for Arsenal, Declan Rice hit the post, fine margins that shouldn’t be impossible to squeeze in our favour. Make ’em wider, thicker.

In the end though, I think the bottom line is quality of personnel. Over the last few seasons the only front three player we’ve had who looked like he could become top, top quality was Bukayo Saka. He was certainly on that trajectory until injuries became a real hindrance, and we saw that this season there were modifications made to his game to make him more effective. I know the discourse around him was a little polarised, but I saw a player more involved, who looked sharper and capable of producing the kind of volume that made him so impactful.

Saka isn’t one of those who finishes every chance he gets, he’s a guy who just keeps going until he makes something happen. The hamstring injury, and then the ongoing Achilles issue made it harder for him to contribute, but I really was encouraged by his season until the injury he sustained against Bayern. And it’s interesting to me that while it might be the kind of player he is anyway, we’ve basically asked Noni Madueke to replicate ‘Old Saka’ in terms of that kind of volume of shots and crosses. He’s had 11 shots across the last two games, and perhaps a single goal from those appear to be a scant return, I think it’s how we need him to play and how Arsenal can maximise what we’ve got up front.

There was an interesting comment on the Arses yesterday wondering how it is that Mikel Arteta can coach and improve defenders and midfielders so well, but not do the same with his attacking players. Some will say it’s because he’s a coach who is defensively minded and this is his wheelhouse. This is what he’s good at. Make a great defence, build a solid midfield in front of them. Perhaps there’s an element of truth in that, but for me it’s down to the players he has to work with.

Sources indicate that if the raw ingredients are good, the recipe has a much better chance of being good, regardless of the talent of the chef. If you get to work with players like Ben White, William Saliba, Gabriel, Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard etc, all of whom arrived in at a relatively young age (Rice perhaps the exception because he had a lot of experience, but Arteta has still made him better), you can develop that potential, build relationships, and see that come to fruition on the pitch.

Up front though, I don’t think we’ve had that level of talent. What can you do with a Willian or a Marquinhos? What can you do with a Gabriel Jesus whose knee explodes (perhaps as we saw in those opening few months before injury hit, you could have done a lot more)? Was Gabriel Martinelli’s plateau down to Arteta’s coaching or the player’s ceiling? I think the fact he’s playing now in Saudi Arabia says a bit about that. I think Arteta squeezed a lot out of someone like Leandro Trossard, who arrived at 28 and became a better player than he was at Brighton, but ultimately there are limits. The same goes for our two strikers, Gyokeres and Kai Havertz. On their days, they can get you goals, but there are too many days when they won’t, and I don’t really think it’s a coaching matter.

Industry observers note that we also need to remember that there was a season when Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal scored more goals than the Invincibles did when they won the league in 2004. It’s not as if his coaching, per se, is an impediment to scoring goals – but like anything it’s layered and multi-factored. We had to become more defensive when all of our attackers were basically banjaxed, we still managed to finish second that season when all we had on the bench was a end-stage Raheem Sterling. If that has tipped the balance a little too far the other way, then you can understand it, and Arsenal are the masters of the single-goal margin victory these days.

Recent findings suggest that I think we can do more to score more, I think some of the players we have are capable of delivering more goals and assists, and over the next few months – being realistic about what we might do in January – that’s what we need to lean into. But my gut feeling is that until such time as we have better attackers to work with, this will remain an glitch – and it’s worth saying that noted issue is one we still find a way to achieve success with more often than that.

I’d just like some fat margins once in a while.

By Darren Plant | 27 Nov 2026 17:32.

Andoni Iraola has revealed that Liverpool winger Victor Munoz "wants" to return to training before Sunday's Premier League fixture against Everton.

Liverpool make the short trip to the Hill Dickinson Stadium for the Merseyside derby looking to strengthen their hold of a top-four spot in the Premier League table.

Although Liverpool earned an impressive 3-0 victory at Club Brugge in the Champions League in midweek, an injury to Munoz took the shine off the win.

After the Spaniard was withdrawn in the first half with a knee injury, Iraola hinted that the summer signing was more optimistic over his issue after the full-time whistle.

Nevertheless, speaking at a press conference on Friday, Iraola suggested that Munoz faces a race against time to be available for the showdown with the Toffees.

The former Bournemouth boss told reporters that the Spain World Cup squad member was yet to make an appearance in training.

However, as expected, Iraola reaffirmed that Cody Gakpo would remain sidelined in the short term.

In a recent development, he said: "Gakpo definitely not. Muscle injury. Munoz, good news after assessment but has a massive knock. He has not trained today but wants to try tomorrow. I cannot tell you right now.

Iraola added: "Gakpo, this is normally two or three weeks. He did against Germany, I don't like timelines with injuries but normally you have to give the time to heal.".

Meanwhile, Ryan Gravenberch is likely to miss out with a heel injury. Iraola stated: "It's going to be difficult.

"I cannot say no, but it's difficult, he is dealing with this situation. The vital thing is he is back with no pain to play as free as possible.".

Liverpool are preparing to play their third of 11 matches across three different competitions before the end of 2026.

With Liverpool presently not possessing the greatest strength-in-depth in midfield and attack, it makes little sense to risk Munoz.

Having made seven starts and seven substitute outings, the 23-year-old is a valuable member of the squad, and it would be more beneficial to rest him in an effort for him to feature against Sunderland three days later.
