Gil  are monitoring the fitness of Marvin Elimbi, who is close to recovering from an injury but was not considered ready to feature in the Taca de Portugal victory over Olhanense.

Hector Hernandez made a substitute appearance last time out after missing the previous six matches through fitness problems and could be given more minutes on Sunday as he looks to regain full match sharpness.

Mohamed Bamba also came off the bench in that encounter to make his first appearance for Gil after a 10-month layoff through injury, giving the hosts another option in midfield.

However, Arthur Tchaptchet remains a doubt, having yet to feature for the Roosters this season due to physical discomfort.

With domestic suspensions carrying over into the league, Xeka, Sanchez and Amissah will all miss Sunday's match following their red cards against Felgueiras.

The visitors will also be without Isra Salazar and Fabricio Garcia, who are recovering from ruptured cruciate ligaments, leaving Giao with limited options as he prepares for his first match in charge.

Yanis Begraoui returned from a muscle injury with a substitute appearance against Felgueiras and scored from the penalty spot, making him a likely starter here.

Gil Vicente possible starting lineup:.

Lucao; Esgaio, Moreira, Buatu, Espigares; Prioste, Lausen; Murilo, Garcia, G Martins; Franca.

Estoril Praia possible starting lineup:.

Turk; P Carvalho, Andreou, Ferro, Parente; Holsgrove, Tsoungui; Guitane, J Carvalho, Lacximicant; Begraoui.

Gil Vicente have not been particularly convincing in front of goal at home recently, but their superior league record and greater stability should give them a considerable advantage against an Estoril side still searching for its first competitive victory of the season.

In a recent development, serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

According to recent reports, the rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

In a recent development, only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More key for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

Recent findings suggest that that leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

Industry observers note that it ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti stated afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

It has been revealed that the ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

Recent findings suggest that the count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 06:47 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:49 EST, 26 November 2026.

The female reporter Jude Bellingham defended during an 'intimidating' post-match interview has praised the England star for being 'respectful' and 'well-mannered' as she opened up on the viral incident.

BBC Sport reporter Elizabeth Conway was speaking to Bellingham after Real Madrid's 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday when another journalist interrupted her as she posed a follow-up question, threatening to cut her interview short.

But the midfielder, 23, refused to answer the interferer and instead told him: 'Sorry, she's got one more [question].'.

Bellingham, who scored a sensational long-range goal on the hour mark to put Real Madrid ahead in the Champions League clash, was widely praised after footage of the incident went viral on social media, with fans applauding him as a 'class act' and 'role model for young men'.

Now Conway has added to the praise, stating the experience 'added a whole newly introduced layer to the love people have for Jude'.

Conway had been waiting to speak to the England star in the 'mixed zone' after the match – an area where journalists line up behind a barrier to interview players.

Jude Bellingham has won praise for his 'respectful' and 'classy' treatment of a female reporter.

Industry observers note that BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had been interrupted by a male reporter when asking her second question, leading to Bellingham's intervention. Source: instagram/@elizabeth.conway_.

Recent findings suggest that 'It is utter carnage,' she told BBC Radio WM, opening up on the incident at the Bernabeu. 'Obviously as an English reporter at Real Madrid, getting Jude is exactly what we want, it's gold dust.

Sources indicate that 'Jude very rarely gives interviews, especially in the mixed zone. It is chaos... It's kind of every person out for themselves.

'You've got elbows, you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you.

'I'm one of very, very few female reporters and one of very, very few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so key.'.

Conway admitted the mixed zone can be an 'intimidating' environment and being interrupted is unfortunately a routine part of being a post-match interviewer.

Admitting it was 'so nice' that Bellingham stepped in to stand up for her, she added: 'It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.'.

Conway, originally from Solihull, specialises in Spanish football and is based in Madrid, according to her Instagram, where she has more than 12,000 followers.

She had asked Bellingham in the mixed zone what had gone through his mind when he scored with his sensational effort at the Bernabeu.

'Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,' Bellingham said. 'I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.

'It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it. It was a nice goal and vital for the team being the second goal and gave us control.'.

The England superstar (right) had been in-demand after scoring with a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

After being interrupted and encouraged by Bellingham to pose her second question, Conway asked whether he feels like he is in the form of his life for club and country.

Recent findings suggest that 'My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter,' Bellingham added.

'Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.'.

Conway later shared the exchange on social media, writing: 'Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,' adding a handshake emoji while fans were quick to praise Bellingham for his 'classy' moment.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked his goal, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported the 23-year-old is in advanced talks over a newly introduced Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Bellingham has previously earned plaudits for his treatment of the media, having stopped to speak to a disabled reporter during the World Cup when several of his England team-mates had walked past, taking the time to answer his questions in Spanish.

The Partenopei pushed Manchester City hard in the Champions League, but they are still facing an early European exit; meanwhile, their hosts face a long fight for top-flight survival.

Under Massimiliano Allegri, who replaced Scudetto winner Antonio Conte in the summer, the Campanian club have won just six of their 17 fixtures and are yet to record consecutive wins.

Before heading to Reggio Emilia, history suggests they can finally do so on Sunday: Napoli have lost just one of 12 away games against Sassuolo in Serie A.

Having won each of the last three while scoring 10 goals, they will be strong favourites with the best in-play betting sites.

In fact, such has been Napoli’s dominance at any venue, Sassuolo have lost the last seven league meetings by a staggering aggregate score of 23-2.

That should cause concern for fans of the Neroverdi, as they are yet to keep a clean sheet this season and currently have the worst defensive record in Serie A.

Seven decades have passed since any side avoided relegation after conceding at least 30 goals within 12 matchdays, so the Emilian club already have a mountain to climb.

Despite firing Alberto Aquilani and hiring Roberto D’Aversa during the last international break, they failed to benefit from a ‘newly introduced-manager bounce’ when losing 2-0 to Genoa last weekend.

So, Sassuolo have now lost all of their last six games - including three on home turf - leaving them stuck inside the drop zone.

Each of those strikes were on home turf - though the most recent was during the 2020-21 season - and Berardi should join Sebastiano Esposito and Armand Lauriente in the hosts’ trident attack.

D’Aversa switched to a back three on his dugout debut, but it remains to be seen if that experiment will continue this weekend.

Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (838 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.
  • In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.
  • Still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," said Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.

In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.

Still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," said Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement. Denmark is leading the way across all four categories assessed — energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and national climate policy. A total of 15 states, including Lithuania, Chile, and Morocco, received an overall "high" rating, which is two more than last year.

The European Union also moved up a spot, while Hungary jumped 21 places after the ousting of former prime minister Viktor Orban's government, which had repeatedly vetoed EU climate looks, dismissing them as a "utopian fantasy.".

The top three positions on the CCPI remained vacant again this year, as no country has yet done enough to meet global climate goals aimed at preventing worsening weather extremes and climate damage.

Recent findings suggest that "We are seeing a striking contrast," said Burck. "Progress on climate action is often slow and in some countries, such as the United States, things are even moving backwards. But technologically and economically there is enormous momentum.".

It has been revealed that that momentum is apparent in record solar energy growth. Last year 75% of global electricity demand growth was met by the green energy source, according to energy think tank Ember's latest global electricity review. Investment in clean energy has also outpaced that in fossil fuels for multiple years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The rapid expansion of renewable technology, as well as the Iran War and a reduction in deforestation are behind a projected slight fall in emissions for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the CCPI.

"Governments have to act now to turn the momentum into sustained emissions reductions," said CCPI co-author Niklas Höhne of the NewClimate Institute, which compiles the report with environmental NGO Germanwatch.

Burck attributed Germany's worst ever performance in the category of national climate policy to current policies being pursued by Germany's economy minister Katherina Reiche.

"Measures that primarily aim to increase the use of natural gas, threaten to undermine progress in the energy transition and risk significantly worsening the conditions for renewable energy and electrification for many years to come," remarked Burck.

A European Commission report published on November 9 on the sidelines of the UN COP31 climate summit in Turkey stated Germany was one of nine EU countries set to miss 2030 emissions reductions targets.

It has been revealed that germany is not alone in its disappointing ranking. The other G20 countries — the world's leading industrialized and emerging economies, responsible for around 80% of global CO2 emissions — also perform poorly.

The only exception among them is the United Kingdom, which ranks seventh and received a high rating, performing well in greenhouse gas emissions, energy use and climate policy. However, study authors rated it low for renewable energy expansion.

The G20's oil- and gas-producing countries occupy some of the lowest positions on the climate action table. The United States, which is the world's second largest emitter, languishes alongside Russia, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Canada around the bottom of the league, with an overall rating of "very low.".

It has been revealed that the hosts of this year's COP31, also received a "low" overall score. Australia, a major coal exporter with some of the world's highest per-capita emissions, ranks 54th, while Turkey, which is also heavily dependent on fossil fuels, comes in 53rd.

China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases and ranks 56th in the CCPI, receiving an overall rating of "very low." Its main weaknesses include its now high per-capita emissions and substantial energy consumption.

However, among the G20, China leads the way in renewable energy expansion. The country, which is five years ahead of schedule in reaching its goal of adding 1,200 GW of wind and solar capacity to the grid by 2030, also produces over 80% of the world's solar panels.

Several oil-producing countries, including Kazakhstan, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates, are also performing better than expected in the renewables category and "are significantly expanding their previously limited" capacity, mentioned the report.

The authors remarked these countries have significant potential to further expand renewables.

It has been revealed that "In the Arab states in particular, very high per-capita emissions and an above-average level of electrification coincide with a relatively low existing share of renewable energy and enormous solar potential," remarked co-author Natalie Pelekh in a statement. "These are, in fact, ideal conditions for more ambitious climate action.".

This article was originally published in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 27 Nov 2026 18:38.

Aiming to remain unbeaten under their new permanent head coach, Lyon welcome Monaco to Groupama Stadium for a Ligue 1 clash on Sunday night.

Les Gones were held to a frustrating draw in the Europa League on Thursday night on home soil, whilst Les Rouge et Blanc enjoyed a last-minute success on their Conference League travels.

Since the arrival of Spanish head coach Carlos Vicens to replace the departed Paulo Fonseca in early November, Lyon have kept back-to-back clean sheets, winning 1-0 at Lille in Ligue 1 last weekend before a draw in the Europa League on Thursday night.

Les Gones were heavy favourites to secure their third League Phase triumph of the season against Lillestrom earlier in the week, however, the French hosts were held to a goalless scoreline, despite posting 22 shots across the 90 minutes.

Since Fonseca left the club to join Sporting Lisbon, Sunday's hosts Lyon have won just one of their past four competitive matches (D2 L1), sitting in fourth position in the Ligue 1 standings after 11 top-flight fixtures.

A cause for Decines-Charpieu optimism ahead of this weekend's clash, Les Gones are unbeaten across their opening five league matches at Groupama Stadium (W4 D1), with only Paris FC picking up more home points in the division to date.

With Endrick returning to Real Madrid over the summer and Pavel Sulc right now sitting in the medical room with a knee injury, Lyon are struggling slightly on the attacking front, firing blanks in three of their past six games.

Whilst this weekend's hosts dropped points in the Europa League on Thursday night, Monaco were busy securing a last-gasp victory in Edinburgh, Scotland, where a star of the 2026 World Cup shone once again following a difficult start to the club term.

United States international Folarin Balogun bagged a brace - including a 94th-minute winner - during Les Rouge et Blanc's 3-2 success at Hearts last time out, with Filipe Luis's side now topping the Conference League table after four matchdays, still boasting a 100% record.

On the contrary to their dominance on the continent, Monaco are winless across their past six Ligue 1 contests (D4 L2) - a stark difference to the start of the league campaign, when they enjoyed a six-game unbeaten run.

As a result of their dipped domestic form, Les Rouge et Blanc have dropped to eighth position in the Ligue 1 rankings and sit three points behind Sunday's opponents Lyon in the lowest of the Champions League spots.

With the aforementioned Balogun failing to reach his previous heights this term after an emotionally-taxing end to the summer transfer window, Paris Brunner is leading Monaco's forward line in Ligue 1 with four goals so far.

Monaco form (all competitions):.

As mentioned earlier, Czechia international Sulc is right now sidelined for Lyon, with the attacking midfielder expected back in the Latest Year.

A graduate of the Liverpool academy, Englishman Tyler Morton is out until February due to a groin problem.

Les Gones also have fitness concerns in defence, with Clinton Mata unavailable for up to a fortnight owing to a muscular injury.

Ansu Fati's road to career resurrection in Monaco has been hindered by a hamstring problem sustained at the end of November.

With the Spaniard set to miss the majority of the December schedule, defender Mohammed Salisu (knee) has a teammate on a similar recovery timeframe.

Greif; Athekame, Bacher, Niakhate, Abner; Bidstrup, Tessmann, Tolisso; Nuamah, Nakamura, Merah.

Monaco possible starting lineup:.

Hradecky; Sane, Dier, Teze; Vanderson, Camara, Zakaria, Nazinho; Minamino, Abline; Brunner.

Scoring 11 goals across four consecutive home league wins since early September, Lyon will be confident of extending their unbeaten run under newly introduced boss Vicens on Sunday.

Monaco have lost just two competitive matches since Luis joined the club over the summer, although we believe that a third defeat is on the cards at Groupama Stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

It has been revealed that spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and fresh signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Industry observers note that como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

The table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

It has been revealed that the refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

Recent findings suggest that his strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

In a recent development, pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

According to recent reports, the sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

Industry observers note that if Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

It also floats a surprise swap that would send Gusto to Liverpool and reunite Alonso with Jeremie Frimpong, his former Bayer Leverkusen right wing-back.

Recent findings suggest that his strength is defending, with 73 tackles and 36 chances created in 45 appearances last season. The weakness is end product, because three goals and five assists are modest for a wing-back who must supply Alonso’s right-hand width.

With no European football this season, Chelsea don’t need that many right-sided options anyway.

Sources indicate that the money matters too. Both players have contracts until 2030 and similar valuations, so a straight swap brings Chelsea no cash and leaves Liverpool with their problem solved.

Sell Gusto instead, preferably abroad, since Paris Saint-Germain have been linked and Chelsea are reportedly open to cutting their asking price. Then spend that fee on a defensive midfielder or centre-back, because that is where Alonso’s team needs help.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

Recent findings suggest that the interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

According to recent reports, scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Industry observers note that not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for significant chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

Latest Update: Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the newly introduced refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

According to recent reports, the trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

It has been revealed that the contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

It has been revealed that the case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

In a recent development, the run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

Recent findings suggest that the schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a fresh flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining presently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

Man City facing fresh Gianluigi Donnarumma dilemma despite Enzo Maresca's public backing

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (649 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 18:46.
  • Manchester City are reportedly facing questions over Gianluigi Donnarumma's suitability for Enzo Maresca's tactical system, despite the Italian head coach repeatedly defending his first-choice goalkeeper in recent weeks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 27 Nov 2026 18:46.

Manchester City are reportedly facing questions over Gianluigi Donnarumma's suitability for Enzo Maresca's tactical system, despite the Italian head coach repeatedly defending his first-choice goalkeeper in recent weeks.

Donnarumma established himself as City's number one following his arrival from Paris Saint-Germain in 2025, but his ability to contribute to the team's build-up play has become a subject of debate.

The goalkeeping department could therefore represent another area for City to assess as they consider how to strengthen Maresca's squad over the coming transfer windows.

According to The Athletic, Donnarumma is not considered an ideal fit for the style of football City are looking to implement, particularly due to his limitations in possession.

The report also suggests that second-choice goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is not viewed as a suitable long-term replacement for the Italy international, meaning that any change between the sticks could require another investment in the transfer market.

However, there is no indication that City have debuted a search for a latest goalkeeper or made a decision to part ways with Donnarumma.

Sources indicate that manchester City are short of a striker and have been since the summer, when they sold Omar Marmoush and did not replace him. #164670. DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's key.

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (935 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's key.

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black?
  • Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?
  • Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black? It seems like it's not doing anything. But it's not doing nothing. It's syncing your messages, updating apps and running other background processes.

Your brain has its own version of that.

Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?

Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.

It's going over your memories, shaping your sense of who you are, imagining possible futures, helping you understand other people and connecting ideas.

That's your brain's default mode network.

Scientists conducted brain-imaging experiments in the 1990s and early 2000s to find out which regions of the brain were active during demanding tasks, like solving a math problem or memory exercise.

But to measure that, they needed a so-called baseline. They needed to know the level of brain activity at rest and during demanding tasks.

So, between the tasks, they asked participants to relax, close their eyes, stare at a fixed point on a wall, or try not to think of anything at all.

And they measured the participants' brain activity both when they were solving a task and doing nothing. That's how scientists noticed the brain was active in up- and downtime.

According to recent reports, they noticed that when participants started to focus on a newly introduced task, after having done nothing, some brain areas lit up and other areas dimmed down. That suggests those areas that dimmed down must have been active while the participant was apparently — physically and mentally — at rest.

This realization eventually led to the discovery of the default mode network or DMN.

The DMN is crucial because it helps your brain make sense of your life and experiences.

It helps you connect and revisit memories, reflect on who you are, imagine what might happen in future scenarios, understand other people, build meaning from experience, and connect ideas in new ways.

Recent findings suggest that it turns all your memories, experiences, knowledge, emotions and social information into your internal story. Think of that story as a constantly evolving, updated model of who you are and how you engage with the world around you.

But it's key to understand the DMN involves more than one area of the brain. It is a group of brain regions that light up when you're not focused on an external task.

There's another player in your brain that acts as a monitoring system. You can think of it as constantly asking "Is there anything that needs my attention?".

Imagine you're daydreaming while driving, and a car suddenly swerves into your lane.

In a fraction of a second, your daydream disappears and your attention snaps back to the road. That player is called the salience network, or SN.

The salience network helps you notice key signals, like a sound, a mistake, pain, an emotion, a threat, or something happening in your body, and helps shift the brain toward attention and control systems when action is needed.

The DMN, SN and attention/control systems constantly interact.

And the DMN doesn't just turn off completely with every hard task. Parts of it can also contribute when tasks involve memory, stories, meaning or other people.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Smartphones have filled many of the small empty moments of our days — waiting for the bus, standing in line, eating alone, lying on the couch. We are constantly looking at our devices.

So, it seems reasonable to ask: are we crowding out those moments of boredom where DMN kicks in?

Maybe. But so far, there's no strong evidence that scrolling directly affects mental health by reducing DMN time.

What we do know is that problematic smartphone use can increase stress, anxiety, task-switching and disrupt sleep.

And sleep loss and stress also have clearer evidence for altering DMN-related brain connectivity.

The DMN is not always necessarily good.

When your mind wanders, it might produce a great fresh idea.

Industry observers note that but it might also replay an embarrassing thing you did five years ago. Again. And again.

In depression, the self-reflection part of the DMN can get caught in repetitive negative loops that are hard to stop — what's known as rumination.

According to recent reports, scientists have also found that Alzheimer's disease targets key DMN areas, particularly those responsible for your autobiographical memory and remembering other aspects of the past. Which may help explain why memory problems are so central to the disease.

Protect your sleep and take stress seriously. There is direct evidence that sleep loss and stress disrupt DMN-related connectivity.

Take real, quiet breaks after mentally demanding tasks, like studying. It can even help you memorize facts for your exam.

Embrace boredom and enjoy doing nothing.

Try to reframe boredom as this essential, energy-intensive active work in your brain that builds your internal narrative and sense of self, consolidates memories, creates connections and sparks creativity.

In a recent development, try waiting in line without checking your phone. Look out the window next time you take the bus or take a walk without listening to anything.

Industry observers note that you can also try scheduling DMN time. It may be the closest thing to a real brain hack.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab oversaw the match between United Arab Emirates' side Al Jazira and Iran's Gol Gohar in Asia's second tier club competition.

Controversy emerged in the 32nd minute after Hattab awarded a free-kick after a foul by Al Jazira's Felício Milson.

Hattab initially waved away protests from Al-Jazira players and approached Milson holding a yellow card.

The official then stunned players after appearing to receive a message in his earpiece, before turning and walking towards Al-Jazira goalkeeper Ersin Destanoglu.

Hattab revealed the goalkeeper a yellow card, despite him being nearly half the pitch away from the incident.

Referee Hanna Hattab was accused by a manager of 'being drunk' following a controversial decision in an Asian Champions League Two match - a claim the official has denied.

The referee was then seen speaking to his fourth official, leading to him rescinding the goalkeeper's yellow card while Milson escaped being shown a second yellow card for his challenge.

Al Jazira scored the only goal of the game minutes later through Anderson Talisca, but the bizarre incident involving Hattab was reportedly the centre of discussion at half-time.

Gol Gohar head coach Mehdi Rahmati had reportedly been seen shouting 'he's drunk' at the official, while the club's sporting director claimed post-match they would have refused to play the second half had Hattab remained in charge.

'The referee against Al Jazira was not in a normal state, and even Al Jazira's players told us the same thing,' noted Heydar Afsari.

'The club immediately informed the match officials and warned them that we would not play if the situation remained the same.'.

Hattab was ultimately replaced by the fourth official for the second half of the match.

The referee, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing pool, has since released a statement hitting back at the allegation.

'I will wait for the official communication and official stance from the Syrian Arab Football Federation, and I will also communicate with the people and parties responsible for me locally and internationally, before issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened,' Hattab wrote.

The claim had centred on the referee appearing to listen to his earpiece and changing his mind on booking an Al Jazira player, before bizarrely showing a yellow card to their goalkeeper.

Al Jazira's goalkeeper appeared stunned by his yellow card, which was later rescinded with the referee then being replaced at half-time of the match.

'In conclusion, I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands.

'Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them.

'I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.'.

Omani sports journalist Issa Stated, who covers Asian competitions, also came to Hattab's defence and insisted the claim the official was drunk is false.

'What happened to him was due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus,' he wrote on social media,.

'He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating.'.

The Syrian Football Federation added in a statement: 'Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media- that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded.

'The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident.

'In this regard, the Committee has contacted the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to request the referee’s medical report, the match commissioner’s report, and the referee assessor’s report, in order to accurately ascertain the facts of the incident and take the necessary follow-up actions.'.

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

His form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has remarked the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

In a recent development, yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

This will be the first top-flight meeting between the two sides, and Kocaelispor arrive in better form, unbeaten in their last five matches across all competitions, recording three wins and two draws.

Their latest league outing saw them hold Fenerbahce to a 2-2 draw, as they overturned a goal deficit only to concede in stoppage time in what could have been a famous victory.

Before that result, Kocaelispor recorded a 2-0 away victory over Eyupspor, a goalless draw against Rizespor, a 3-0 win over Mazidagi Fosfatspor in the Turkish Cup and a 2-1 away victory against Alanyaspor.

The weaknesses show elsewhere: no assists, three chances created in 781 minutes, seven completed dribbles at a 25% success rate and 43.8% of duels won. FotMob values him at about £47m.

Schade would add depth, but he wouldn’t add what Arteta lacks: a winger who beats his man and drags two defenders with him against low blocks.

According to recent reports, nusa builds his game on exactly that, and his output at Leipzig now justifies waiting until next summer. Schade’s returns suggest he would sit behind a fit Tzolis, which is hard to justify at a price Brentford would set after already refusing an approach.

A bid becomes sensible only if Tzolis breaks down again or Leipzig block Nusa completely, because Schade needs no time to adapt to the Premier League. Even then, anything above £50m would pay for potential rather than production, and a 25% dribble success rate tells Arsenal he isn’t the specialist they need.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Industry observers note that not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and said needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.

Pochettino’s trust is a real advantage, since he knows exactly what work rate he gets, but trust doesn’t turn a 28-year-old with one league goal this season into a £28m solution to a defensive crisis. Juventus also just rewarded him with a contract to 2030, so they have no reason to sell cheaply.

Sources indicate that romano mentioned Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the same breath, and each offers more control from midfield. If Pochettino wants a familiar face, a rotation option on a short deal makes sense. Spending about £28m on a runner does not.

In a recent development, zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. It has been revealed that an Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Recent findings suggest that çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

It has been revealed that the location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

According to recent reports, tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Industry observers note that çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

Venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

By Joshua Cole | 27 Nov 2026 19:12, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 19:14.

Fenerbahce will aim to strengthen their position in the upper half of the Turkish Super Lig table when they welcome BB Erzurumspor to Chobani Stadium on Sunday.

The hosts sit sixth with 20 points from 12 matches, while the visitors are 13th on 14 points and are looking to end a three-match losing run.

Emre Belozoglu's tenure at Fenerbahce has been impressive so far, with the team remaining unbeaten under his leadership after playing four matches across all competitions.

His tenure kicked off with a 3-2 win over Liverpool in the Champions League before the Yellow Canaries recorded a 5-0 away victory over Corum.

That result preceded a 2-2 draw against Kocaelispor in the league, the only game they have failed to win under the manager so far, but they promptly returned to winning ways in midweek when they beat Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 away from home.

However, there is still plenty of work to do for the Yellow Canaries in the Super Lig, as they are already 11 points off the top, having failed to win half of their dozen league games so far this season (W6, D2, L4).

Despite those dropped points, Fenerbahce have been the division's most productive attacking team, scoring 31 goals, and they will hope to overwhelm their opponents with their attack as they look to bounce back from defeat in their last home league game, when they lost 2-1 to Goztepe.

Further reason for optimism will be the hosts' record in this fixture, having faced Erzurumspor six times without defeat and winning their last five meetings.

Erzurumspor, meanwhile, have suffered three consecutive league defeats after a promising run earlier in the campaign, losing 1-0 to Goztepe last time out, having previously been beaten 2-1 by Caykur Rizespor and 3-1 at home by Corum.

This recent poor streak follows an encouraging run of four matches without defeat, during which they won three times and drew once while keeping three clean sheets, a far cry from their last three matches, in which they have conceded six goals.

Serkan Ozbalta will be concerned about his team's poor run extending, not only because of their unfavourable head-to-head record with Fenerbahce, but also their away record this season, with just one win in six matches on the road, losing three times and drawing twice.

Erzurumspor have also struggled to prevent the Yellow Canaries from scoring, having conceded at least two goals in their four visits to this ground, with at least three scored in each of the last three, all of which they lost.

Mason Greenwood has scored in three of the last four matches and is expected to play an important role from the start yet again, while Vedat Muriqi will hope his goal in the Champions League earns him a starting spot over Romelu Lukaku once more.

Erzurumspor have no confirmed absentees listed ahead of the match, although their final selection will depend on fitness assessments closer to kickoff.

Gyrano Kerk and Ibrahim Diabate started as the front two last time out and are likely to retain their places for this one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham transfer news: Tottenham Hotspur are one of four clubs tracking Hakan Calhanoglu, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Italian outlet lists Galatasaray, Juventus and Como alongside Spurs, although it gives no detail on how far Tottenham’s interest has progressed.

In a recent development, the timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January. Inter want to extend but are trimming wages for their over-30s. Calhanoglu earns roughly £5.7m a year, and Inter are discussing £4.4m plus bonuses. He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

Calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob highlights three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

Passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

According to recent reports, roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

Spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

CalcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

It has been revealed that his strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

It has been revealed that the weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

No, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Maresca has used Nico O’Reilly in midfield this season, yet O’Reilly started only seven of City’s first 15 games while managing a back problem, so an available specialist left-back is no luxury. Khusanov, Nunes and Guéhi all picked up knocks at Forest, which leaves the back line short.

In a recent development, city should treat the Juventus talks as a pricing exercise. A straight loan sends a 25-year-old on a contract until 2030 away for six months and returns him no more valuable, so only a loan with an obligation to buy close to the £31m fee makes sense.

It has been revealed that otherwise, give him a league start, see whether his attacking threat helps a side that keeps conceding, and let Maresca’s evidence decide. A club that paid £31m for a left-back last year has not shown he cannot do the job; it has shown only that the manager prefers somebody else.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 27 Nov 2026 19:12.

Eyupspor will be hoping to end their prolonged winless run when they welcome Istanbul Basaksehir to Esenyurt Necmi Kadioglu Stadium on Sunday.

The hosts are bottom of the Turkish Super Lig standings with just three points from 12 matches, while the Grey Owls sit seventh with 20 points and will be looking to continue their push towards the European places.

Mustafa Dalci has been unable to turn around Eyupspor's fortunes this season, with the Purple-Yellows enduring a difficult start to the campaign and remaining without a league victory in their last nine matches.

No other Super Lig side is on a longer losing streak than Eyupspor, who have lost each of their last nine league games, while they have failed to score in 10 of their 12 matches, netting just three times, the fewest in the division.

They are also comfortably the worst side defensively, having conceded 31 goals, three more than the next-worst defence, while they are presently on a two-match run without finding the net.

Their latest setback was a 1-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, and on Sunday, they welcome an opponent they have never beaten in four top-flight meetings, losing two and drawing two, leaving little optimism as they look to end a club-record run of consecutive Super Lig defeats.

Basaksehir, meanwhile, have enjoyed a much more encouraging run and arrive in Istanbul's western suburbs having won their last three league matches.

Their latest victory was an entertaining 4-2 home triumph over Corum, with Bertug Yildirim scoring a hat-trick after coming off the bench to help his side secure all three points as they came back from a two-goal deficit, scoring all four goals in the final 13 minutes plus stoppage time.

That result followed a 1-0 victory against Goztepe and a 2-1 win over Kocaelispor, with Nuri Sahin's side demonstrating greater consistency and attacking confidence in recent weeks, scoring more goals than any other side over the last five games (13), while only three teams have accumulated more than their 12 points over that period.

The Grey Owls will also be confident of winning consecutive away matches, having ended their four-match winless run on the road (D1, L3) with victory over Goztepe on their last trip.

Eyupspor form (all competitions):.

Istanbul Basaksehir Turkish Super Lig form:.

Eyupspor are expected to be without Lenny Pintor, Talha Ulvan and Simone Giordano, who are all dealing with injuries.

Their absences could limit Dalci's options, particularly in defence and the attacking positions, while Yusuf Barasi could be considered for a starting role as the hosts look for greater threat in the final third.

Basaksehir will be without Christopher Operi, who remains sidelined with an injury, while Yusuf Sari is also unavailable.

Yildirim's hat-trick against Corum could earn him a starting opportunity, although Davie Selke remains an option in attack.

Eyupspor possible starting lineup:.

Bilgin; Yasar, Demir, Jules; Costa, Akman, Ilter, Raux-Yao, M. Demir; Abdullahi, Barasi.

Istanbul Basaksehir possible starting lineup:.

Sengezer; Karbownik, Opoku, Bayram, Kharebashvili; Kemen, Kaluzinski; Olsen, Shomurodov, Brnic; Yildirim.

Eyupspor may attempt to keep the contest close through a compact defensive approach, but their prolonged winless run and Basaksehir's attacking quality point towards an away victory.

The visitors should have enough to secure three points without necessarily needing to produce another high-scoring performance.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested.
  • In a recent development, the interest makes sense.
  • FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested. The 21-year-old Portugal forward has scored 11 goals in 11 Serie A games since joining from Benfica B in July. Barcelona are equally keen, Inter watch him live at every match, and Napoli are reported as his strongest Italian suitor.

In a recent development, the interest makes sense. Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals. Arsenal’s results haven’t suffered, but their number nine position has produced little.

Finishing is the selling point. FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes. The weaknesses are just as clear: he wins 34% of his duels, completes 41% of his dribbles and ranks in the ninth percentile among forwards for defensive contribution, which clashes with the pressing Arteta wants from his striker.

In a recent development, di Marzio indicates Monza will listen at around £22m to £26m, with the money earmarked for other signings, after paying about £3m including bonuses. Flashscore reports Benfica hold a 20% sell-on and a right to match offers, and Varela’s agents meet Monza this week.

Yes, but in the summer and only if Gyokeres leaves. Arsenal’s results are strong, so a January rush for a 21-year-old would add risk without fixing a crisis. A fee near £26m looks modest beside the £64m Gyokeres cost, and Varela’s goals-per-game record argues for the gamble far more than Gyokeres’ two in 15 does.

The real risk is suitability. He also scores for a struggling side, so his chances come in games unlike most of the Premier League games Arsenal play. Arteta needs a number nine who presses and wins duels, and Varela does neither well, so Arsenal would be buying a finisher and building the rest of his game themselves.
