The Serie A disciplinary judge suspended no players after matchday 12, so neither Juventus nor Como lose anyone for Sunday's game. Como were fined again for a slow restart, and Juventus head to Lake Como five points behind them.

Juventus travel to Como on Sunday with no suspension worries. Nor do their hosts. Serie A disciplinary judge Gerardo Mastrandrea banned nobody after matchday 12 in a ruling published in Milan on 24 November.

The decisions covered the games of 21, 22 and 23 November. Nobody was sent off across the round. No player one booking from a ban picked up a yellow card either.

Recent findings suggest that juventus had no cards from their own fixture. The club’s match sheet for the 4-0 win over Venezia at the Allianz Stadium lists no bookings, with Arena as referee.

All four goals came after the break. Woltemade (53′), Koopmeiners (59′) and Cabal (65′) scored before Kolo Muani converted a penalty (71′).

Two Lecce players, Danilo Veiga and Jamil Siebert, picked up their fourth booking of the season and are now one caution from a ban, Virgilio Sport reported. No Juventus or Como player reached that threshold this round.

According to recent reports, como did not escape the judge entirely. The €8,000 fine was imposed under strict liability for delaying the start of the second half by about four minutes without good reason. The judge treated it as a repeated repeat offence.

Sources indicate that it was the largest of the round’s penalties for late restarts. Fiorentina and Milan were also fined as repeat offenders. Genoa received €3,000 for a two-minute delay to kick-off.

Recent findings suggest that the problem is not new for Como. In the previous round, the communiqué of 10 November fined them €10,000, again as repeated repeat offenders. On that occasion the second half started about two minutes late.

According to recent reports, juventus were not blameless that week. The same 10 November ruling fined them €5,000 for holding up the start of the first half by the same margin as Como’s latest delay.

The match carries weight in the race for the top four. Como have 8 wins, 2 draws and 2 defeats from their 12 games. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

It has been revealed that juventus have 6 wins, 3 draws and 3 defeats. Their attack, with 19 goals, has almost kept pace with Como’s. The difference lies at the back, where Juventus have conceded 12.

Sources indicate that A win on Lake Como would narrow the gap to their hosts. Defeat would push Juventus further from the top four.

Como host Juventus at the Sinigaglia on 29 November.

  • In a recent development, and Mourinho was keen to underline the impeccable state of mind of his player, who does not seem disturbed by his status in the Madrid offensive hierarchy.
  • In a recent development, but the José Mourinho show really began when a journalist asked him if he was considering combining Kylian Mbappé and Carlos Espí at the forefront of his attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that josé Mourinho had a lot to say after Real Madrid’s stunning victory over Celta Vigo. Jostled by the Galicians, the Merengues had to fight to snatch a precious success thanks to Bellingham and Carlos Espi. A more complicated meeting than expected for the Portuguese technician, who notably pointed out the fatigue of his internationals and the lack of concentration of his team at the start of the match. But at the press conference, the Special One especially put on a show when discussing his offensive choices. Asked about Carlos Espí, who continues to be decisive despite limited playing time, Mourinho explained at length the qualities of his striker. “He’s a surface player. When you dominate an opponent who is content to defend, his game is devastating. He has quality in the area, he plays with his back to goal, he is good with his head, he attacks both posts… He has all the qualities of an area player. History is full of players like him, decisive even with limited playing time”he noted.

In a recent development, and Mourinho was keen to underline the impeccable state of mind of his player, who does not seem disturbed by his status in the Madrid offensive hierarchy. “We are happy with him. He’s the kind of player who doesn’t get distracted by discussions about his playing time: Should Kylian be a substitute or play more? He knows that he is progressing, that he has the respect of the coach, his teammates and the supporters. He is happy. And I hope to have the opportunity to give him tenure, 90 minutes or more”continued the Portuguese. A way of also justifying the use and playing time of Carlos Espi with a Madrid team rather focused on offensive transitions and depth.

In a recent development, but the José Mourinho show really began when a journalist asked him if he was considering combining Kylian Mbappé and Carlos Espí at the forefront of his attack. A possibility that Mourinho does not completely rule out, but which would pose serious balance problems for his team. And the Portuguese technician found a rather original way of explaining it. “I can do it, but when we lose the ball, I, being on the sideline, will have to enter the field in transition and punch someone to stop the counter-attack! Because playing with two pure strikers means the wingers have to defend inside. And it will certainly not be Diomandé, Vinicius, Arda… A little Brahim, perhaps. But with the characteristics of our wingers, we are not made to play in a classic 4-4-2”he noted. Behind the joke, Mourinho insisted on the tactical constraints of such an association. “It’s more complicated than you might think. It’s easier for the supporters, as well as for you. But the reality is a little more difficult. ».

Finally, José Mourinho also took advantage of this press conference to end the suspense concerning Vinicius Junior. While questions surrounded the presence of the Brazilian in the starting lineup during the next meeting in Madrid with his goals for Brazil during the break, the Special One preferred to cut short speculation with his usual humor. “I stated it yesterday, it doesn’t matter whether he’s a substitute or a starter. To avoid you asking me the question on Monday and having too much to say, I’m going to be a bad boy and end the story: he will start Tuesday in the Champions League.he announced. An answer which has the merit of being clear, while Mourinho wants to juggle and alternate between offensive positions. And after a difficult victory against Celta Vigo, the Madrid coach recalled that at Real Madrid, aligning all the offensive talents was not necessarily enough to build a balanced team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sebastian Sternik | 27 Nov 2026 23:14, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 23:22.

Hoffenheim will be looking to build on their impressive comeback win over Sturm Graz in the Europa League when they welcome Augsburg to the SNP Arena this Sunday evening.

Consistency has been a major issue for Die Kraichgauer in recent weeks, while the visitors recently snapped a seven-match winless run in the Bundesliga.

Balancing domestic and European duties has proved difficult for Hoffenheim, who have endured a mixed start to the season.

Christian Ilzer’s men enter the weekend 11th in the standings after losing six of their 10 Bundesliga games, equalling their club record for defeats at this stage of a campaign.

November has been more encouraging, however, with Hoffenheim drawing away at Crystal Palace, losing at Eintracht Frankfurt and winning their last two home games against Schalke and Sturm Graz.

Thursday’s victory over the Austrian side was particularly impressive, as Hoffenheim came from behind to win 3-1 and move within three points of the Europa League’s top eight.

That was also their fourth consecutive home victory, with three of those wins seeing them score exactly three goals.

While the hosts are beginning to build momentum, Ilzer faces some difficult selection decisions after injuries and suspensions decimated his defence, leaving him with just one natural centre-back.

Augsburg may not be flying high in the Bundesliga table, but they have at least found themselves among the league’s elite in one rather unexpected ranking.

Manuel Baum’s side sit second according to online portal Bild Dating’s AI-generated beauty leaderboard, which rates the attractiveness of every squad in the German top flight.

Their on-field fortunes have been a lot less glamorous, though a 3-1 victory over Mainz 05 last time out lifted Augsburg to 10th in the actual standings and brought an end to their seven-game winless run in the Bundesliga.

The win over Mainz also saw Baum receive a straight red card for delaying play in the second half - a punishment which will see him rooted to the stands on Sunday.

Assistants Alexander Frankenberger, Frank Frohling and Felix Kling will share touchline duties in Hoffenheim as Augsburg look to claim just their second win in 11 meetings with the Kraichgauer.

The trio will take charge of a youthful Augsburg side that made club history against Mainz, fielding their youngest-ever starting XI with an average age of just 23.7 years.

Six players in the team were aged 21 or under - a stat which underlines the extent of the club’s ongoing injury problems and the responsibility placed on their young talents.

Hoffenheim form (all competitions):.

Augsburg form (all competitions):.

Hoffenheim’s main concern is the suspension of Ozan Kabak, who received a four-match ban for grabbing Eintracht Frankfurt’s Oscar Hojlund by the scruff of the neck and pushing him to the ground.

Hoffenheim have lodged an appeal, though Kabak remains suspended from league action until Friday’s hearing, where the punishment may be cut short or potentially extended.

This is a massive blow for Ilzer, who is already missing four other defensive players in Wouter Burger (muscle), Valentin Gendrey (broken leg), Albian Hajdari (foot) and Robin Hranac (knee).

In fact, Japan’s Koki Machida remains the only available natural centre-back in the squad.

Augsburg are also dealing with a lengthy injury list, although Calvin Brackelmann is available again after returning from his absence.

However, Han-Noah Massengo and Jeffrey Gouweleeuw remain out of action with muscular problems, while an infection has disrupted Noakhai Banks’ recovery.

Chrislain Matsima is making progress from a torn muscle but is not yet ready to return, potentially opening the door for 18-year-old Tim Schnitzer to retain his place after impressing against Mainz.

Hoffenheim possible starting lineup:.

Baumann; Coufal, Machida, Bernardo, Rots; Avdullahu, Lenz; Conte, Asllani, Prass; Lemperle.

Augsburg possible starting lineup:.

Dahmen; Keitel, Bah, Schnitzer; Fellhauer, Wolf, Rieder, Behrens; Kade, Claude-Maurice; Gregoritsch.

Hoffenheim have defensive concerns, but their formidable home record against Augsburg should give them confidence, having lost just one of their last 15 Bundesliga meetings on their own ground.

Augsburg, meanwhile, have lost their last three away league games and, with several senior players unavailable, could struggle to avoid another defeat against their bogey team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, long chains of sugars known as polysaccharides support many biological functions, from strengthening tissues to modulating cell signalling. Synthesizing these compounds in the laboratory with precise lengths and architectures, which are needed to establish how the structures of polysaccharides affect biological behaviour, has been difficult. Writing in Nature, Yin et al.1 now report an enzyme-based strategy that produces highly uniform polysaccharides and enables chains to restart growth after consuming all of the sugar building blocks in the reaction, once more sugars are added. The authors achieved this control by adjusting how readily an enzyme binds the small sugar molecules that are used to initiate the growth of each chain.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that juventus captain Manuel Locatelli has called his knee injury one of the hardest spells of his career. Answering questions from young members of the club, he stated his recovery is on track and that he has learned to live with a long wait.

Manuel Locatelli has not played since early September, and the Juventus captain admits the time away has been tough. Speaking in a newly introduced episode of the club’s Junior Reporter series, in which children from the Juventus membership programme interview a first team player, the midfielder was open about how he is coping.

As ANSA reported on Tuesday evening, Locatelli put the injury alongside Italy’s failure to reach the World Cup as the lowest points of his time as a professional.

Locatelli explained that he hurt his knee and now has to stay off the pitch for a long time. He noted he feels good and that the work is going well, much of it in the gym rather than on the grass.

“I miss playing football so much, so much, but I have learned to accept this situation,” he told the young reporters, according to the quotes carried by Calciomercato.com. He added that he knows he has to give it time, and that he must do his best to come back in good shape.

On the national team, he did not hide the pain of missing out on the tournament. “When you lose, and lose like that, it is a moment of suffering,” he noted.

The problem dates back to 6 September, when Locatelli sprained his right knee in the 1-1 home draw against Milan. Two days later Juventus confirmed in an official medical enhancement that he had undergone surgery in Lyon to suture the external meniscus. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the operation with club doctor Marco Freschi in attendance, and rehabilitation started the following day.

The club gave no return date at the time. ANSA now indicates the captain expects to be available again in the first months of 2027, while Football Italia reports that he is not expected back in full training before March.

Locatelli also spoke about leadership. He said becoming captain was an ambition he had from the moment he arrived from Sassuolo in 2021, and he credited Giorgio Chiellini, Leonardo Bonucci and Danilo for showing him what it means to be present for the group every day. His childhood idols, he said, were Pavel Nedved, Gianluigi Buffon, Alessandro Del Piero and Francesco Totti.

The club tied him down in April, when he signed a new contract until June 2030.

His absence has forced Luciano Spalletti to reshape his midfield for most of the autumn, a problem we looked at when Thuram and Locatelli were both missing earlier this month.

According to recent reports, juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday on the back of a 4-0 win over Venezia, and go to Como on Sunday with a clean bill on the disciplinary front, as covered in our piece on the matchday 12 rulings. Their captain, for now, remains a spectator, but by his own account a patient one.

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a upcoming low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick mentioned: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”.

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

Industry observers note that “First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”.

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he remarked.

In a recent development, carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”.

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but mentioned he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

Sources indicate that “It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he remarked. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”.

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

In a recent development, “I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick remarked. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

Sources indicate that “I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s key we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”.

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

Sources indicate that “There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”.

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

According to recent reports, whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a massive reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for several weeks already, his fate had been sealed. Michael Carrick was finally dismissed from his position this Thursday, after meeting his now ex-leaders the same morning. Omar Berrada, the general manager, and Jason Wilcox, the football director, informed him of the end of the adventure, three days after the announcement of his imminent departure. It is this method that is being singled out today by the press and observers, more than the dismissal of the Manchester United coach. The situation was becoming inevitable.

According to recent reports, while he knew he was doomed since Monday morning, the day after the draw at Old Trafford against Aston Villa (4-4), the technician continued his mission, biding his time. His representatives had been contacted by management to announce their intentions to separate. Except that in the meantime, Berrada and Wilcox hopped on a plane to Monaco to meet the club’s co-owner, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and finalize the details together. Only returning to Manchester on Wednesday evening, they then called Carrick to arrange a meeting the following morning.

According to The Telegraphthis way of doing things and this very long wait upset the former midfielder. He did not understand why he had to organize the sessions on Tuesday and Wednesday, without most of the management players, who had left for selection, but with his assistants: Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, all fired since yesterday. At the same time, MU was working on the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino. In this tense context, made of mutual reproaches and delaying tactics, the information inevitably leaked.

It has been revealed that “Over the past 24 to 48 hours, the situation has been catastrophic. While the manager, a club legend, directs training on the field, the management and owner are in Monaco, and simultaneously contact the American Football Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino», jumps Gary Neville in the still very popular podcast, Stick to Football by The Overlap. “It’s simply sickening. This is well below the standards expected in any other tech giant, in any other industry. This would be unfair dismissal and you would be prosecuted», Continues the former Mancunian defender.

“Being in Monaco while the team, the staff and the people who manage the club on a daily basis are in Manchester is very frowned upon, and it casts a negative light on the management. I don’t think anyone will come out of this unscathed.» Strong words which echo those made the day before by Peter Schmeichel, another legend of the Red Devils of the 90s. «If they look for someone else, let them relieve him of his duties! Don’t let him come and lead the training. He did it again yesterday (Wednesday). How disrespectful is that?», asked the former goalkeeper.

According to recent reports, faced with Carrick’s anger, management tried to defend itself, again according to The Telegraph. She understands the frustration of the 45-year-old technician and regrets that their separation happened like this. She also denies having carried out all the checks (notably legal) prior to and necessary for dismissal, before communicating her decision to the person concerned. The club believes it has demonstrated all possible transparency. These explanations will not convince many people as Manchester United is used to these procedures. The dismissal of Amorim, for example, is less than a year old….

According to recent reports, the race for the FIFA presidency is entering its home stretch. While Gianni Infantino intends to run for a latest mandate during the election scheduled for March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco, the opponents of the outgoing president still have a few days to find a candidate capable of bringing their challenge. The deadline for submitting applications is set for November 18, i.e. Wednesday, and UEFA is working to present a profile likely to unite its 55 member associations. A delicate mission for the European body, which has been looking for several weeks for a sufficiently influential personality to embody a credible alternative. Meanwhile, the Italian-Swiss leader is increasing diplomatic trips and seduction operations with the various confederations to consolidate his lead, at a time when Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japanese Football Federation, is also a candidate.

Industry observers note that however, the avenues have multiplied in recent weeks without really coming to fruition. As we revealed to you exclusively this morning, UEFA once considered supporting Luis Figo, with the idea of ​​banking on the notoriety of the former Portuguese international to lead the battle against the FIFA president. An option which was not ultimately unanimous within the European body. Other names have also been circulating, starting with that of Arsène Wenger, director of world football development at FIFA, whose possible candidacy would have required a spectacular change of position. The former Arsenal coach would have ultimately declined this possibility. Didier Drogba and Mikaël Silvestre were also mentioned, without these avenues materializing. Faced with these successive refusals and the urgency of the timetable, European leaders must now make their choice.

Recent findings suggest that according to information from Guardianconfirmed by RMC SportPhilippe Diallo could finally be the surprise candidate chosen by UEFA to challenge Gianni Infantino. The president of the French Football Federation, in office since 2023, would have taken a step ahead of the other contenders and his candidacy could be made official on Tuesday. The UEFA executive committee must meet to examine this possibility and seek the approval of the 55 member federations. The choice of a French leader would mark a change in strategy for Europe, which initially hoped to rely on a personality with greater international notoriety, from the field or the sidelines. Philippe Diallo, however, presents the profile of an experienced administrator and has gradually established himself as one of the most assertive opponents of Infantino. Last September, he considered that the initiatives of the FIFA president during and after the 2026 World Cup had seriously damaged the image and unity of football, considering that trust was broken.

In a recent development, it now remains to be seen whether this candidacy can really shake up Gianni Infantino who maintains a very favorable position. Philippe Diallo could count on the support of the vast majority of European associations, but also try to convince several French-speaking federations of the African Football Confederation. A job of persuasion which promises to be particularly complicated, since the outgoing president benefits from numerous relays on the African continent and in other confederations. According to RMC SportInfantino would already have 80 to 90 votes acquired from the votes expected in March 2027. Philippe Diallo’s lack of international notoriety also constitutes a serious handicap, despite his weight within French and European football. THE Guardian also underlines that the multiplication of opposing candidates could ultimately serve the interests of the outgoing president, who would have an easy time presenting himself as the candidate of unity in the face of a divided opposition. The possible appointment of the boss of the FFF would open a latest chapter in this political battle, without guaranteeing UEFA the ability to shake Gianni Infantino.

Latest Update: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even introduces?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1095 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.
  • More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.
  • Industry observers note that in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.

More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.

Industry observers note that in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost. And since 1990, nearly 490 million hectares of forest have been wiped out.

More recently, the trend has shifted in the opposite direction. Deforestation in the Amazon region of Brazil decreased by 41% from August 2025 through 2026 to reach its lowest rate since records began.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

To ensure lasting protection, the Tropical Forest Forever Facility was launched in 2025 at the COP30 climate conference in Belem, Brazil.

Because rainforests are so key for the world, the idea behind the fund was to give money to the countries where they are located to help them preserve and protect these ecosystems.

So far, these countries have made more profit through deforestation — for example, by mining natural resources on rainforest land or farming the area.

Recent findings suggest that starting in 2027, the TFFF is expected to generate the funds needed for rainforest conservation, in part via contributions from various countries. By the end of this year, a total of $10 billion (€8.9 billion) in government capital is due to flow into the fund, mainly in the form of low-interest loans.

In addition, the TFFF is expected to glitch bonds to private investors, such as banks and investment firms, to raise additional funds — initially totaling about $40 billion.

In a recent development, going forward, the blueprint is for governments to contribute a total of $25 billion to the pot, and for private donors to contribute $100 billion. The fund will then invest this money in international financial markets with the aim of generating profits.

Private investors who purchase TFFF bonds can expect to earn about 5% interest per bond per year, remarked Felix Finkbeiner, the founder of the German environmental organization Plant-for-the-Planet, where he is responsible for forest conservation and advocacy.

"Private investors' capital is very well protected," Finkbeiner remarked, adding that any losses the TFFF might incur on the capital markets — for example, if the price of its bonds should fall — would be offset by government funds.

About 2.7% of the TFFF's profits would be set aside for countries with tropical forests.

Countries would receive $4 per year for every hectare of forest that they preserve instead of chopping down. At least 20% of these funds must be allocated to Indigenous peoples and local communities.

According to calculations by the TFFF Watch website, an independent platform introduced by Plant-for-the-Planet to track investments, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for example, would receive about $333 million for its 2024 forest stock under this system.

Finkbeiner said the subsidies would be paid only for intact ecosystems and not for timber plantations, with forest areas and their condition mapped and assessed using satellite imagery. Though it can sometimes be difficult to identify plantations accurately on satellite photos, he said, the technology has improved significantly over the last decade.

It has been revealed that that means any NGO or external party with access to the satellite data can check the condition of the region, providing further oversight. If forest areas are cleared or damaged, money is deducted from the total.

Another safeguard: If countries don't use the TFFF funds for rainforest conservation, their payments could be frozen for the next few years.

Industry observers note that the TFFF is supposed to invest, whenever possible, in government bonds issued by emerging and developing countries. Above all, the idea is not to invest in projects that harm the climate — such as those linked to oil, gas, or coal investments.

The TFFF concept has received plenty of support from environmental organizations, in part because it gives countries in the Global South significantly more sovereignty than traditional forms of development financing.

"For example, if the government of Ghana wants to protect its rainforest today, it usually asks the World Bank for financial assistance — and then the World Bank in [Washington] DC decides whether Ghana is allowed to do so," Finkbeiner said.

According to recent reports, the TFFF fund is also designed to be immune to donor countries' backing out in the event of a change in government, for example. Once a contribution is made, the money remains in the fund for 40 years before being paid back.

Continuing protection is also an incentive for countries receiving money from the fund. "When a new government comes into power that wants to cut back a little on climate protection, they will realize: We'll get more money if we protect the rainforest," mentioned Finkbeiner.

In a recent development, for the rainforest fund to actually get off the ground, a total of $10 billion in seed capital must be raised by the end of 2026. So far, the confirmed pledges from countries, NGOs and foundations total only $7.9 billion.

Eight countries have expressed a willingness to contribute so far, including Brazil, Indonesia, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

Sources indicate that norway, with a pledge of $3 billion, is the largest would-be donor. However, the government in Oslo is willing to honor its commitment only if the agreed-upon total amount is in place by the end of the year.

"This deadline isn't set in stone, but otherwise the Norwegian government will have real trouble getting it through parliament," Finkbeiner remarked.

Germany's commitment must also still be approved by the parliament. The German government has pledged about €1 billion to the TFFF starting in 2027, to be paid out over 10 years.

Other countries are also considering investing in the TFFF, including Canada, China, South Korea and the United Arab Emirates.

Philanthropic organizations have pledged $88 million to the fund so far, including $73 million declared this week during the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. Finkbeiner remains upbeat.

It has been revealed that "Promises like that always come at the last minute," he noted. "I'm very optimistic that we'll secure more commitments at the COP — and in the course of December — and that we'll then reach that $10 billion.".

This article was originally written in German.

Footage appears to show Bruno Fernandes created the divot in the turf that led to his fortunate second goal against Sporting Lisbon.

The Manchester United captain scored a bizarre goal against his former side on Wednesday night, with his long-range shot taking a fortuitous bobble off the Estadio Jose Alvalade pitch to leave goalkeeper Kaique Pereira helpless.

While fingers were initially pointed at the ground staff, footage shows the divot was actually created by Fernandes himself when he planted his boot into the turf while pressing high up the pitch moments earlier.

Reminiscent of former Liverpool forward Stan Collymore's famous bobbling goal past Blackburn Rovers goalkeeper Tim Flowers in 1996, Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

The goal summed up another chaotic evening for United, in which goalkeeping calamities, controversial refereeing calls, three penalties and a red card resulted in a 2-2 draw and left them 19th in the Champions League standings.

United trailed at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens saved one penalty before conceding another 75 seconds later that was converted by Luis Suarez after the Belgian's reckless challenge on Max Araujo.

Fernandes' speculative effort would undoubtedly have been easily gathered by Pereira had it not struck the bump in the turf.

Lisandro Martinez, who had given away the first penalty, won one at the other end that Fernandes converted before the former Sporting star fired in the long-range effort that bounced over Pereira and into the net.

More drama followed as Lammens flapped at a cross under pressure from Suarez, allowing the striker to score, before Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have put undue pressure on Pereira when forcing an own goal from the goalkeeper.

United were left frustrated by what they viewed as a lack of consistency after Marciniak was sent to the pitchside monitor to review the second decision, and their mood darkened further when Youri Tielemans was sent off for a second booking late on.

Alisson Becker will start in goal this weekend, shielded by a centre-back duo of Jeremy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk, the latter coming off the bench during the Reds' 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

Flanking the duo should be Ronald Araujo at right-back and Milos Kerkez on the left, with the Hungarian being singled out for praise by his manager after a strong defensive showing.

With Gravenberch a doubt due to a heel fascia issue, Dominik Szoboszlai is likely to start alongside Alexis Mac Allister at the base of midfield, while youngster Trey Nyoni is an option as a substitute.

Florian Wirtz has delivered a slew of immense performances in recent weeks, and will be operating in the number 10 role on Sunday, keen to add to his man-of-the-match display in the 4-0 triumph over Manchester United with another against Liverpool's derby rivals.

Iraola will be breathing a sigh of relief that winger Munoz avoided a serious knee injury during the Reds' win in Brugge, but Cody Gakpo remains sidelined due to a calf problem, so expect to see Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola start out wide.

Alexander Isak will lead the line at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, hoping to build on his brace in Belgium earlier this week.

Liverpool possible starting lineup:.

Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Nyoni; Barcola, Wirtz, Ngumoha; Isak.

RB Leipzig is off to an excellent start to the 2026-2027 season. Sitting in fourth place in the Bundesliga standings, Martín Demichelis’ men display a particularly attractive face, driven by very effective offensive animation. Despite the resounding departure of Yan Diomandé, who left to join Real Madrid for 140 million euros, the Saxon club has not lost its offensive drive and continues to showcase its firepower. With 32 goals scored after ten days, Leipzig confirms that they will have to be counted on in the race for the top places. An offensive success which owes a lot to the emergence of Brajan Gruda.

It has been revealed that at 22, the German has established himself as one of the revelations of the start of the season. Impactful, creative and endowed with excellent technical quality, the left-hander makes a difference thanks to his dribbling, his changes of pace and his ability to eliminate in small spaces. Indisputable in the offensive sector of RasenBallSport, Gruda already has 3 goals and 6 caviars in 14 appearances. Revealed in Mainz, passed through Brighton before returning to Germany last February, he quickly convinced Leipzig to extend his loan for the current season and has established himself as one of the most formidable attackers in the Bundesliga in recent months.

Aligned on the right side of the attack, he brings his ability to unbalance opposing defenses and necessarily recalls Yan Diomandé, his predecessor in this position. With 27 successful dribbles, he is the best player in the Bundesliga in this exercise according to statistics published before the 10th day. His importance was further demonstrated against Union Berlin this weekend, as he provided an assist before finding the net himself in the 5-1 victory. His trainer Martín Demichelis does not hide his affection for him: “I love this boy, I have a good relationship with him, both as a player and as a person.”.

But it was also in the Mannschaft jersey that the young attacker made his mark during the last rally. Called up by Jürgen Klopp, Gruda perfectly negotiated his first two selections in November, with two goals and two assists against Serbia (3-1) and the Netherlands (5-0). Against the Serbs, he scored a spectacular goal after a solo run from his own half, before doing it again against the Dutch. Four decisive contributions in two matches, a remarkable performance which leads us to believe in a bright future for him with the Mannschaft. Klopp was full of praise for him, calling him a “real street footballer” and hailing him as an exceptional talent. A recognition which confirms the change in dimension of Gruda, now as important in club as in selection. RC Lens, who faces Leipzig this Tuesday, has been warned.

According to recent reports, como beat AEK Athens 1-0 to reach 12 points in the Champions League, despite eight unavailable players and a late drop in intensity. Juventus visit the Sinigaglia on Sunday, but must first play Omonia on Thursday.

The narrow victory over AEK was Como’s third straight win in the Champions League. It leaves them close to the knockout stage. It also offers the latest look at Juventus’s next league opponents, on the same ground.

The win came with a stretched squad. Fàbregas told Sky Sport that the absentees were either injured or left out of the Champions League squad list. Making so few changes was, he stated, a first in his coaching career. That is a thin bench ahead of a league weekend.

Sources indicate that the scoreline flattered AEK in places. Lucas Da Cunha missed a first-half penalty, and Nico Paz hit the post. At the other end, goalkeeper Robert Sánchez made two important saves before the break. Milla’s goal made him the 11th different player to score for Como in this season’s competition. No other team in the Champions League has had that many different scorers. UEFA named him Player of the Match.

Sources indicate that como had been scoring freely before Matchday 5. On Matchday 4 they won 9-1 away to Lens, a result that put them fourth at the halfway point of the league phase. AEK proved a harder problem. They held Como up for long spells and were difficult to break down.

Recent findings suggest that the final stretch was the concern. Fabio Capello put it to Fàbregas that Como had dropped off badly in the last 20 minutes. The coach replied that he did not yet have the experience to stay calm in such moments. The late fade is consistent with a group short on fresh legs.

It has been revealed that fàbregas also set out his priorities. He mentioned the win brought Como close to at least a play-off place, but that qualification was not yet secured. In the same breath, he stressed that Serie A matters more to the club. That message points straight at Sunday’s meeting with Juventus.

Juventus have their own European commitment first. Kick-off in Turin, in the Europa League league phase, is at 20:00 UTC. Juve go into that game fifth with 10 points from four matches. Omonia are 18th with six. Sam Barrott of England will referee, with Darren England on VAR.

It has been revealed that that schedule cuts into any advantage from Como’s fatigue. Both sides will carry European minutes into the weekend. Juve, however, will have had two fewer days to recover.

The league table adds weight to the fixture. Como sit fourth in Serie A, eight points ahead of Juventus. A home defeat would leave a depleted Como squad with a reduced cushion. A Juve win would close the gap at the end of a demanding week.

Como’s Champions League campaign continues away to Real Betis on 9 December, and the league phase ends with a trip to Barcelona on Wednesday 27 January 2027. After Sunday’s 13th-round meeting at the Sinigaglia, Juventus host Udinese at 18:00 on Sunday 6 December.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Sources indicate that enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

Sources indicate that however, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

Everton: Jack Grealish apologizes after his disciplinary sanction

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jack Grealish has decided to break the silence after several complicated weeks at Everton.
  • This exclusion followed a violation of the club’s disciplinary regulations.
  • Manu Tournoux is a passionate and knowledgeable football enthusiast with a special focus on French football.

Jack Grealish has decided to break the silence after several complicated weeks at Everton. Left out of the squad by David Moyes for missing training without permission, the 31-year-old England international publicly apologized to supporters and club members. Thursday evening, after returning to the field during a friendly match played behind closed doors against Derby County, the player on loan from Manchester City published a message on Instagram to acknowledge the situation and show his desire to return. “ Glad to be back on the field with the guys today after a good few days of training! I would like to apologize to the supporters and all members of the club for not being able to help the team in recent weeks “, he wrote, accompanying his publication with several photos of the meeting. Grealish also reaffirmed his attachment to the Toffees: “ I love playing for this club and I can’t wait to play in front of you again in an Everton shirt. See you soon! » A speech which comes as the former Aston Villa player has not played an official match since the defeat against Chelsea (0-2) on October 17.

This exclusion followed a violation of the club’s disciplinary regulations. After initially citing illness to justify his absence during the trip to Arsenal, Grealish was sanctioned by Everton, notably missing the matches against Newcastle and Coventry City. David Moyes, however, left the door open for his return, specifying that a decision would be made with the managers when the player could be available again. On Thursday, the Englishman took a first step by participating in Everton’s victory against Derby County (4-1) during a friendly meeting organized at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Alcaraz scored twice, while Jonathan Nsangou and Christian Norgaard also scored. Returning for a second consecutive loan after a first season disrupted by injury, Grealish is still looking to relaunch his career away from Manchester City, who recruited him for more than 100 million euros in 2021. With only six appearances this season before his sanction, the attacking midfielder now hopes to regain the confidence of David Moyes and rapidly reintegrate the professional group.

Industry News: Rare gene variants can affect a person’s height by up to 17 centimetres

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.
  • Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.
  • Industry observers note that an analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Human height is determined almost entirely by an individual’s DNA.Credit: XinXinXing/Getty.

Rare mutations that prevent proteins from functioning can have a surprisingly large effect on people’s height, researchers have found.

Industry observers note that an analysis of more than 1.4 million people’s protein-coding DNA has identified hundreds of genes that affect people’s height. The work also uncovers previously unrecognized biological mechanisms that underly human growth.

The findings, published on 25 November in Nature1, might help with the development of treatments that mitigate height changes caused by some medical conditions, such as forms of dwarfism.

“The impact these genes have on any given individual can be massive in terms of accurately predicting their height or making sure they’re getting the right treatment for a disease,” says Adam Locke, a statistical geneticist at the Regeneron Genetics Center in Tarrytown, Upcoming York.

About 80–90% of variation in adult height is caused by genetics. Projects analysing common gene variants have mapped thousands of DNA changes that can influence height. For example, a 2022 study identified more than 12,000 common genetic variants that collectively accounted for 40% of height variation in populations with European ancestry2.

However, how rare genetic variants (those found in less than 1% of a population) affect people’s height is less well studied.

To systematically probe how rare variants contribute to people’s stature, Locke and his colleagues gathered DNA and height data. In total, they looked at sequencing data from more than 1.4 million adults. They analysed the protein-coding sections of DNA and ran a series of tests to spot non-random links between height and both common and rare gene variants.

Sources indicate that the analysis uncovered rare variants in 207 genes, which, on average, were linked to a height difference of about two centimetres. The team also identified 17 genes that had a particularly strong effect on height. The variants associated with this gene set all resulted in the production of non-functional proteins. In the study, over 700 people had at least one of these loss-of-function variants.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

Genetic study homes in on height’s heritability mystery.

Individuals carrying such a variant were, on average, about nine centimetres taller or shorter than were people who didn’t have that variant. The strongest effects included a 17-centimetre reduction in height associated with a change to the ACAN gene and an 11-centimetre increase linked to the FBN1 gene. These effect sizes are more than 50 times larger than those of most genes commonly associated with height.

“We would expect rare genetic variants that disrupt gene function to have larger effects than common genetic variants, but the magnitude of some of these effects is particularly striking,” states Andrew Wood, a statistical geneticist at the University of Exeter, UK.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan went into their Europa League fixture against Olympiacos in need of a win to get the ball rolling, and win they did.

In a recent development, the eventual 2-4 scoreline only tells part of the story, as Ruben Amorim’s side had to battle back from two goals down. Lorenzo Pirola’s header drew what was officially an own-goal from Mike Maignan, then Jota Silva doubled the lead after a slack pass from Koni De Winter was punished.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then came the Omari Hutchinson show. The Englishman gave Milan hope with a wonderful solo goal, before turning provider for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround. Diego Moreira’s late goal on the counter made sure of a very vital three points.

In a recent development, so, the Diavolo return to Italy with smiles on their faces, cultivating the hopes of a play-off spot and keeping the top eight dream alive too. Ivan Stoev has picked out five major talking points from a dramatic night on the outskirts of Athens.

Omari Hutchinson has had mixed performances when given the opportunities since his arrival in the summer and the feeling is that he had plenty of work to do in order to justify the hefty optional price tag on his loan contract. Games like the one against Olympiacos are just the type of opportunities for the attacker to prove his abilities.

The Nottingham Forest loanee didn’t get off to the best start as Milan struggled in the opening 45 minutes with their opponents pressing very high and aggressively. This starved him of possession in a central role and he didn’t get the ball to his feet much, let alone with space to run at.

In the second half, however, Hutchinson moved to a wider role on the right flank and he immediately started causing trouble for the Greeks.

In the 56th minute it was an impressive solo run by the Englishman that started Milan’s comeback as the winger picked up the ball in his own half and carried it all the way to the opponent’s penalty box, before cutting onto his left foot and beating the keeper with a tidy finish in the far post.

Sources indicate that milan fez uma grande reviravolta na segunda parte em casa do Olympiacos, com Omari Hutchinson em destaque. https://t.co/RsOgYVqrP7.

— B24 (@B24PT) November 27, 2026.

Seven minutes later Hutchinson continued to cause trouble down that flank. This time around he found Cisse with a lovely cross and the youngster made no mistake to bury it and bring the scores level.

The former Arsenal academy man wasn’t finished yet though: in the 71st minute he provided yet another inviting cross into the penalty box which found Pulisic, who applied a lovely volleyed finish to make it 3-2.

Recent findings suggest that hutchinson then continued to be a menace in transition as he revealed relentlessness even in the dying minutes. A corner was cleared and he picked up possession, somehow beat a man and ran with it, getting the ‘hockey assist’ for Moreira’s goal.

According to recent reports, it was an absolutely brilliant second-half performance and if he finds continuity then that option to buy might just before more appealing, or at the very least a re-negotiation to keep him permanently. The matter is that the Olympiacos owner also owns Forest, and he saw that display first-hand.

In a recent development, the goals Milan conceded were quite preventable yet again. The feeling is definitely growing as January approaches that the back line needs a true leader in the middle of a defence that continues to be error-prone.

In a recent development, mario Gila has looked like a bargain of a signing and he has been superb, but he is playing mostly as a right-back/outside centre-back. Strahinja Pavlovic remains a key player as well, but the same applies as with Gila just on the left side.

Koni De Winter is just not a man that you can trust to anchor the rearguard to a high level most weeks. He’s had some stellar performances – the game against Inter comes to mind – but he often follows up those performance with some shocking ones.

Matteo Gabbia is definitely better in terms of leadership and keeping things tidy, but we will need to wait and see if he features in Amorim’s long-term aims. He’s been injured for quite a while too, so a reacclimatisation period will be required.

It has been revealed that sankhoun Diawara also looked very shaky in Greece, but this in itself proves a point because the idea cannot have been for him to start as many games as he has. It just further signals that someone who can play down the middle and steady everything could be the difference this season and beyond.

Ardon Jashari got his first Milan goal at the weekend in the win over Frosinone. Then, the unfortunate injury to Luka Modric leading up to the Olympiacos game meant he was given the chance to prove himself, after a few shaky performances this season.

Excluding a few misplaces passes in the first half, the Swiss international was solid enough. There wasn’t anything flashy but also no errors leading to goal, which was a relief. The stats say that he had 77 touches, completed 58/64 passes (91%), had 1 big chance created, 2 tackles, 7 recoveries and 1 clearance. He also won 2/2 aerial duels and 2 ground duels, committing just 1 foul.

Speaking of chances being seized, it’s worth giving a shoutout to Fikayo Tomori who came on for a struggling De Winter. Milan looked much more solid with the Englishman on the pitch as he showcased his athleticism but also his experienced reading of the game.

The professionalism shown by Tomori must be respected given the centre-back was excluded from the squad in the summer and put on the transfer market. He worked hard to prove that he deserves to stay and to play. Now, the next mission is to earn what right now seems like an unlikely renewal.

In the first half Milan were struggling with the high press and the limited space, so they had limited chances going forward. The second half was a completely different story especially with Yunus Musah and Pulisic coming on for Estupinan and Goncalo Ramos.

According to recent reports, we have already mentioned Hutchinson ran the show, but Pulisic was also crucial as he scored an impressive volley which is hard to execute by any standard,  and he then goal the assist that made the final 4-2. He should’ve really scored another one, but we’ll give him a well-earned pass.

It has been revealed that moreira was also heavily in the mix and at times he was frustrating with his end product being lacking, though the direct nature of his pace and dribbling were a joy to watch again. Having a player who picks up the ball and claims ‘Fine, I’ll do it’ is really refreshing. His defensive effort as a wing-back was not lacking either.

Cisse all in all had a quiet game yet found his name up in lights on the scoreboard for a 10th time this season with a tidy headed finish. The knack that he has for being in the right place at the right time is something that is so impressive in a 20-year-old. A pay rise could be on the way to fend off calls from England.

Industry observers note that we have to give the coach his flowers too, don’t we. The first half wasn’t good but it was still better compared to some other European performances this season. The goal was very preventable, but the Rossoneri did well not to fold under the pressure Olympiacos were applying.

In the second half the coach made two changes which improved the team quite a bit, though one of them was forced as Ramos was injured. Amorim revealed after the game that he knew the Greek side couldn’t keep up their high press for 90 minutes, which would yield spaces to attack in the second half.

In a recent development, shifting Hutchinson to the right was also the correct choice, as was taking off De Winter for Tomori, and also letting Cisse play as a centre-forward. Depending on how Ramos is, he might have to do the same in Cagliari.

Finally, it is worth mentioning the attitude was completely different as opposed to the game against Ferencvaros. The desire and belief that the game could be turned around offers some encouragement that this team cannot just get into the knockout stages, but can give anyone a game if they show up.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.
  • This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (BIG) campaign called "The King's Return.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (BIG) campaign called "The King's Return.".

BIG, a Christian group for footballers, has stated it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

Industry observers note that "Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he noted.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

According to recent reports, "I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.".

He then said that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

In Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.

"We feel well prepared," Klopp said, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

According to recent reports, klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.

"We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

According to recent reports, from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

Sources indicate that “Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, stated of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

It has been revealed that “I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

Industry observers note that the same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Industry observers note that konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

According to recent reports, konsa, 29, has rapidly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

Industry observers note that the victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also states plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his upcoming surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

According to recent reports, “Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

According to recent reports, “I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

It has been revealed that “I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

Madueke should do better. Rice finds him and the winger drives into the box. He takes a shot but drags a right-footed effort wide.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

George is looking lively for Everton. He tries to come inside and whip an effort to the far corner but the ball deflects wide.

From the corner, Gabriel clears off the line after Raya loses track of the ball.

Sources indicate that everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

Recent findings suggest that everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any intends to sit deep and play on the counter.

According to recent reports, set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

According to recent reports, arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

According to recent reports, A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Recent findings suggest that horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

On bouncing back from defeat...

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

Recent findings suggest that “They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

Industry observers note that “Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”.

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

In a recent development, this is right now Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Industry observers note that today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz.

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Sources indicate that arteta noted: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Recent findings suggest that moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.
