  • According to recent reports, neto last played for Juventus in May 2017, when he was part of the side that beat Lazio 2-0 in the Coppa Italia final.
  • His most recent competitive outing came on 30 May with Botafogo, as Football Italia noted after Wednesday’s press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that norberto Neto is set for his first competitive game in almost six months when Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday night. Speaking on the eve of the match, the 37 year old goalkeeper said he still felt he had unfinished business in Turin.

According to recent reports, neto last played for Juventus in May 2017, when he was part of the side that beat Lazio 2-0 in the Coppa Italia final. More than nine years on, the Brazilian is in line to start again in black and white, with first choice Guglielmo Vicario being rested for the visit of the Cypriot side to the Allianz Stadium.

His most recent competitive outing came on 30 May with Botafogo, as Football Italia noted after Wednesday’s press conference. Since then he has been working as cover, a role he took on after joining as a free agent at the end of September.

In a recent development, juventus moved for Neto after Kamil Grabara ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in training on 19 September, only days after keeping a clean sheet on his debut against NEC. The club confirmed his return on 28 September with a contract running until 30 June 2027.

Asked what drew him back, Neto explained that he had been looking for a next step that genuinely meant something to him. “Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open,” he mentioned, in comments reported by ilBianconero, which carried the press conference live. He added that he is enjoying his work and is in Turin to help, whatever the coming months bring.

Opening the press conference, he described his feelings simply: “It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team.”.

In a recent development, neto was asked about Vicario, who is on loan from Tottenham and has been Luciano Spalletti’s regular choice in goal. He kept his answer short: “I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper.”.

The veteran also spoke warmly about the younger players around him. He said their eagerness to contribute was infectious and that the squad has the quality, will and determination it needs. On the goals Juventus have conceded this season, he pointed to a side that is still developing, with several players fresh to Serie A and finding their way. His own focus, he said, is on training at full intensity every day while the team looks for balance and consistency.

Juventus go into matchday five fifth in the league phase standings with ten points from four games. Omonia have won two and lost two. Neto warned against taking them lightly, saying they are a strong side who break forward with real quality, and revealed he knows Omonia’s Fabiano from his years in Brazil.

He also stressed that Europe brings its own demands, noting that Juventus always carry a responsibility to compete to win in every tournament they enter.

Interest in the meeting was already strong after ticket sales for Omonia passed 35,000 last week. Next up in Serie A is the trip to Como, where both sides go in without suspensions.

For Neto, the night is a chance to add to the 22 appearances he made in his first spell, when he won two league titles, two Coppa Italia trophies and a Supercoppa Italiana as Gianluigi Buffon’s understudy.

By Nsidibe Akpan | 27 Nov 2026 23:58.

Fortuna Sittard play host to SC Heerenveen in the 2026-27 Eredivisie at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion in Sittard on Sunday.

Heerenveen are sixth on the Eredivisie table on 24 points and Fortuna seventh on 23, with leaders PSV Eindhoven on 29, so Sunday's winner will leave a direct rival for one of the European play-off places trailing in December.

Danny Buijs's side have lost only twice in 13 league games and are unbeaten in seven since a 5-1 home defeat by Ajax on September 12, leaving the Fortunezen seventh on 23 points from six wins, five draws and two defeats.

Both of those defeats, the other being 2-0 against AZ on August 22 with Ole Romeny sent off early, came at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion, whereas Fortuna are unbeaten away from home, with a 1-1 draw at Feyenoord on October 31 featuring an equaliser from Feyenoord loanee Shiloh 't Zand.

Home draws have been the problem, as Fortuna led Twente 1-0 on October 10 through an Anthony Descotte header from a Mohamed Ihattaren cross before drawing 1-1, and led Telstar 2-0 on November 7 through an Ihattaren penalty and a Sem Valk own goal before conceding twice before half time in a 2-2 draw.

Their latest home win was a 1-0 victory over Excelsior on October 25, decided by a Rodrigo Guth header from an Ihattaren corner in stoppage time, when Descotte and Lequincio Zeefuik were unavailable and Ihattaren started on the bench.

The most recent result was a 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles on November 22, when Descotte scored his sixth goal of the season in the 50th minute after Ihattaren sent substitute Kristoffer Peterson clear, ending the hosts' unbeaten home record.

Off the pitch, Buijs revealed on Wednesday, November 18 that he will not extend a contract expiring in 2027 and will leave after four seasons, which leaves Fortuna a little over six months to appoint a successor.

Robin Veldman's De Superfriezen have won their last six matches in all competitions, including five straight in the league against Excelsior (4-0), ADO Den Haag (3-2), NEC Nijmegen (1-0), Feyenoord (5-3) and Groningen (3-1), scoring 16 goals and conceding six.

The 5-3 win over Feyenoord on November 8 ended the leaders' unbeaten league record, with Heerenveen recovering from 2-0 down after 31 minutes through Maas Willemsen, Levi Smans and a hat-trick from half-time substitute Ringo Meerveld in the 61st, 84th and 93rd minutes.

At Groningen on November 21, Dylan Vente scored in the 41st minute after a blunder by goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar and again in the 73rd, with substitute Dirk Proper adding a third in the 80th to secure a first win at the Euroborg since March 19, 2023.

Heerenveen's 27 goals scored and 17 conceded give them a goal difference of +10, nine better than Fortuna's +1 from 21 scored and 20 conceded.

The run followed a September wobble that ended with a 4-0 win at Sparta Rotterdam on September 19 after a five-game winless spell, and the only league defeat since was 2-0 at PSV Eindhoven on October 9.

Heerenveen have also won their last two league games on the road, 3-2 at ADO Den Haag on October 24, when Jacob Trenskow scored twice, and 3-1 at Groningen.

Fortuna have a goalkeeping problem, as first-choice Mattijs Branderhorst sprained an ankle in training before the Go Ahead game and Luuk Koopmans, who made several saves in that 1-0 win, is expected to deputise again.

Buijs is also without attackers Zeefuik and Romeny, who are both expected back around January 8, plus midfielder Edouard Michut, who is due back around December 5, and defender Daley Sinkgraven.

The losses matter because Descotte, Zeefuik and Ihattaren had scored 11 of Fortuna's first 16 league goals before the Excelsior game, which leaves Descotte, Sven Simons and Peterson to carry the attack.

Yassin Oukili is a doubt after a spell out, and Buijs is expected to keep the back-five shape used at Deventer.

Heerenveen have one doubt in defender Hristiyan Petrov, who returned from Bulgaria duty injured, missed the Groningen derby and was still not fully fit on Friday, when Veldman mentioned the club would decide whether he travels.

The rest of the squad trained on Friday morning without problems, no suspensions have been reported, and Veldman is likely to keep the side that won at Groningen, with Mees Hilgers covering at centre-back if Petrov is not risked.

Fortuna Sittard possible starting lineup:.

Koopmans; Van Ottele, Guth, Hubner, Pinto, Dahlhaus; Ihattaren, Brittijn, 't Zand; Simons, Descotte.

Heerenveen possible starting lineup:.

Klaverboer; Braude, Kersten, Willemsen, Zagaritis; Linday, Courtens; Trenskow, Smans, Meerveld; Vente.

Heerenveen have scored three or more goals in four of their last five league games and field five forwards of their own in Vente, Meerveld, Trenskow, Smans and Rivera, whereas Fortuna have lost Zeefuik and Romeny and lean heavily on Descotte and Ihattaren for goals.

Fortuna's unbeaten run and their record of two or more goals in four of the last five meetings cannot be ignored, but they have won only two of six home league games, twice surrendered a lead against Twente and Telstar, and will start a stand-in goalkeeper against a side that has scored 16 goals in its last five league games.

Five of the last six meetings have produced at least three goals, including Heerenveen's 2-1 win on April 25, 2026 and Fortuna's 2-0 win on November 8, 2025, so Descotte should score again, but Heerenveen's depth and momentum make them the likelier side to land the decisive second.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Published: 13:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • The SFA have been forced back to the drawing board for a second time in their efforts to introduce new proposals around youth development.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 13:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 26 November 2026.

The SFA have been forced back to the drawing board for a second time in their efforts to introduce new proposals around youth development.

Led by chief football officer Craig Mulholland, the plans had been geared towards ensuring more Under-21 players in Scotland gain more minutes at first-team level.

The original intends were for two Scotland-eligible Under-21 players to start in domestic cup competitions, and for players to feature for a minimum of six per cent of all available minutes across a season in league campaigns.

When it became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t on board, a new watered-down version was put back on the table.

But the newly introduced proposals have also now been met with resistance — forcing the SFA to kick the can further down the road into the new year.

There will now be no vote on the back of the upcoming AGM, with further discussions required prior to something more concrete coming to fruition for the start of next season.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has been sent back to the drawing board by clubs.

A statement from the governing body remarked: ‘The Scottish FA has been encouraged by the productive dialogue with clubs regarding proposals to harness opportunities for young homegrown talent.

‘The most recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation in order to present a consolidated package of recommendations to an SPFL member vote.

‘The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews, when the reality of our domestic game’s standing in respect of playing time for under-21 players compared to the rest of Europe was made clear.

‘We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game.

‘It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams.

‘We have therefore agreed that the consultation process will continue into the Upcoming Year with the intention of a comprehensive proposal going to SPFL members within the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of William Hill SPFL season 2027-28.

‘The Scottish FA General Meeting to vote on the complementary Scottish Gas Men’s Scottish Cup proposals will now follow a similar timetable.

‘Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right.’.

Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.
  • "There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak remarked after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.
  • "The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.

"There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak remarked after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

"The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".

The threat comes after the Canadian government confirmed Wednesday that it would not allow Russian players to take part in the IIHF World Junior Championship starting on December 26 in Alberta.

"Canada's position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues ⁠its war of aggression ​against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual," Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary of sport, noted in a statement on Wednesday. "Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.".

Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling in late October, in which it remarked the security concerns the IIHF cited for barring Russian teams from taking part in international tournaments was not sufficient, the world governing body pledged to work to comply with the decision.

According to recent reports, on November 8, Norway said it had been bumped from the World Juniors tournament and had been informed by the IIHF that Russia would take its place. Several other national hockey associations said they had received a revised schedule for the tournament and stated they would not play against Russia. The IIHF has not confirmed the change.

Germany has been watching developments related to the World Juniors and host nation Canada closely, as it is set to host the IIHF World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf starting on May 14.

With several nations saying they will not play Russia and major sponsors threatening to pull out, a German government spokesman described the prospect of hosting the tournament under these conditions as "effectively impossible.".

However, Germany has ruled out taking the Canadian approach.

Ronald Rauhe, Germany's minister of state for sport, said Wednesday that refusing to grant visas was "not a solution for the [German] ice hockey federation [DEB], nor is it a solution for successfully hosting a world championship anywhere.".

At the same time, though, he expressed support for the DEB in its wish to host the tournament as planned.

"We believe that we should channel all our energy and efforts into helping sport — and ice hockey in particular — find a solution, which would, of course, entail excluding Russia from the World Championship.".

What makes things even more complicated for German officials are concerns that taking a hard-line on Russia could jeopardize Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

According to recent reports, the thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees bidding to host an Olympic Games to follow its lead. The IOC is set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process.

According to recent reports, for now, though, the ball appears to be in the IIHF's court, after Ottawa confirmed its refusal to grant Russians visas to play in the World Juniors. How the dispute regarding that tournament gets resolved could go a long way to finding a solution for the men's tournament in Germany in May.

Today's Premier League predictions include Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United home debut against Brentford, and Aston Villa's visit to Ipswich Town.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first match at Old Trafford as Manchester United head coach takes place on Saturday afternoon when Brentford visit the Theatre of Dreams for an intriguing Premier League contest.

While the Red Devils occupy a place in the relegation zone, sitting 19th in the Premier League table, the Bees are nine points and 13 places better off in sixth spot after 11 matches.

Despite Man United’s dismal start in the top flight, Pochettino's first Premier League home match in charge should spark enough attacking urgency from the hosts to trouble a Bees side that has struggled on its travels.

Taking into account that each of the last six head-to-head battles has seen both teams score, while 12 of Man United’s last 14 home matches have produced over 2.5 goals, we can envisage a wide-open, end-to-end affair ending all square on this occasion.

Sources indicate that > Man United vs. Brentford preview.

Two teams hoping to build on Premier League victories last weekend meet at Elland Road on Saturday afternoon, as Leeds United play host to Coventry City.

These two teams last butted heads in February 2025 when the Whites secured a 2-0 away victory in the Championship en route to promotion as champions.

With Leeds and Coventry both arriving at Elland Road in high spirits following victories last weekend, all signs point toward an entertaining clash given that five of the Sky Blues' last six league outings have featured at least four goals, and nine of the previous 13 meetings between the two sides have seen both teams score.

While a rejuvenated Coventry outfit will fancy their chances of breaching the hosts' backline, Leeds remain unbeaten on home soil this season and possess more than enough attacking firepower to claim their third league win in a row.

Aston Villa travel to Portman Road to face Ipswich Town on Saturday evening seeking to climb back into the top half of the Premier League table.

Both meetings between these two sides during the 2024-25 season ended in entertaining draws (2-2 in Suffolk and 1-1 at Villa Park), leaving the Tractor Boys still searching for their first top-flight triumph over the Lions since February 1993.

While Portman Road remains a far more forgiving environment for O'Neil’s side, who have collected seven of their 11 points on home soil this term (W2 D1 L2), Villa should relish the opportunity to rediscover their scoring touch against a porous Ipswich defence shipping an average of two goals per game.

Although the Tractor Boys are capable of keeping things competitive in Suffolk, we are backing Emery’s men to shake off their recent slump and grind out a hard-fought victory.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:03 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 15:03 EST, 26 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United were the beneficiaries of a bizarre goal in the Champions League on Wednesday night, as the captain's long-range effort bounced up off the turf and deceived the goalkeeper to help earn Mauricio Pochettino a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in his second game in charge.

Football has certainly seen its fair share of quirky, bizarre and downright bonkers goals over the years, and Fernandes' effort in Lisbon is certainly one to add to the collection.

Here, Daily Mail Sport's reporters look back at some of the strangest goals they can remember, from outrageous goalkeeping blunders to freakish deflections and moments of sheer misfortune.

Darren Bent (Sunderland 1-0 Liverpool) - October 17, 2009.

Forget bouncing in off a divot, try the ball flying into the net off a beach ball. Darren Bent’s winner against Liverpool at the Stadium of Light back in 2009 has got to be the strangest.

A Liverpool fan lobbed a gigantic red beach ball on to the pitch (in the middle of October) which was initially removed by a steward only for the wind to blow it back.

What made it even funnier was that when Bent’s shot struck it, Liverpool keeper Pepe Reina tried to save the inflatable, which now resides in the National Football Museum, instead of the actual ball that flew past him.

Thank heavens there was no VAR back then to spoil the day.

Pepe Reina had no chance after Darren Bent's strike ricocheted off a beach ball into the goal.

Peter Enckelman (Birmingham vs Aston Villa) - September 16, 2002.

In a recent development, obviously the mind immediately goes to balloons and players ghosting behind goalkeepers. But my favourite happened on September 16, 2002 between Birmingham City and Aston Villa.

Olof Mellberg took a throw-in. He threw it back to Peter Enckelman. The ball bounced under Enckelman’s foot and rolled into the Villa goal. Referee David Elleray reckoned he must have touched it with his studs.

Recent findings suggest that it was all made worse for Enckelman with a Birmingham fan hopping out of the crowd to goad him to his face. I must have been nine years old and remember watching all this live.

Can’t imagine my parents told me what that hand gesture the fan was doing in front of Enckelman meant.

Peter Enckelman scored a disastrous own goal after the ball bounced underneath his foot.

Mo Diame (Brighton vs Newcastle) - February 28, 2017.

Brighton half cleared a corner and Christian Atsu returned a scuffed volley, which was helped on by the toe of Daryl Murphy, before Mo Diame planted his foot in the ground and allowed the ball to bounce off the back of his heel, looping up and over all inside the goalmouth and into the top corner.

I was there, and I have revisited my match report.

Recent findings suggest that 'Diame had been stood still for the majority of the previous 81 minutes,' I wrote. 'Finally, it was a tactic which served him well.'.

I also refer to the goal as fluky and hilarious. It is now the stuff of legend on Tyneside, for it helped Newcastle to win promotion as champions. Indeed, without it, Brighton would have finished top and Newcastle second.

Mo Diame scored one of the craziest goals in Championship history against Brighton in 2017.

Tony Popovic (Portsmouth vs Crystal Palace) - September 11, 2004.

Some goals stay with you because of the sublime, others because of the ridiculous. And I doubt I'll ever see a stranger goal live than Tony Popovic's flying backheel into his own net in 2004.

With Portsmouth protecting a 2-1 lead late on against Crystal Palace, nerves were jangling around Fratton Park until Popovic's moment of spectacular misfortune.

It has been revealed that pompey's Steve Stone floated a hopeful cross into the Palace box, prompting Popovic to stretch out a leg in an attempt to clear. Instead, he somehow managed to flick the ball off his boot, onto the post and into the net, producing a finish any top striker would be proud of.

Olivier Giroud, eat your heart out.

Portsmouth couldn't believe their luck when Tony Popovic flicked the ball into in his own net.

Nani (Manchester United vs Tottenham) - October 30, 2010.

This one has always stuck with me, partly for the sheer audacity of Nani and partly because it's the sort of goal that simply wouldn't escape VAR scrutiny today.

Back when a trip to Manchester United was still a fearsome prospect, Spurs were a goal down and chasing a late equaliser when Nani was brought down in the penalty area and appeared to handle the ball.

Crucially, though, Mark Clattenburg had not blown his whistle. Tottenham goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes, assuming a free-kick had been awarded, placed the ball on the ground.

Sources indicate that still gesticulating, Nani got up, realised the ball was still live, and coolly passed it into the back of the net. Cue bedlam in the Stretford End.

Nani celebrates his controversial goal against Spurs, to the fury of goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic (Sweden vs England) - November 14, 2012.

It's not weird in the category of a divot or a beach ball but the most outlandish goal I've ever seen live was Zlatan Ibrahimovic's 30-yard overhead kick for Sweden against England at the Friends Arena in Stockholm in November 2012.

It has been revealed that A long ball came over the top of the England defence, Joe Hart ran out and headed it clear and Ibrahimovic launched himself into the air, hooking the ball in a majestic arc over England's disbelieving goalkeeper. Great goals can be strange, too.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic's acrobatic bicycle kick against England was both strange and sensational.

Stan Collymore (Blackburn vs Liverpool) - February 24, 1996.

As soon as I watched Fernandes' speculative long-range strike bobble past Sporting Lisbon goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, my mind immediately cast back to Tim Flowers being embarrassed by Stan Collymore at Ewood Park in 1996.

Not that it was the Blackburn goalkeeper's fault, of course. Collymore's feeble effort from distance in the 11th minute trickled along the turf before hitting a rogue divot and bouncing over Flowers' head into the net.

Collymore, who cracked a smile but toned down his celebrations, turned away in disbelief as Flowers stared down at the pitch with his hands on his hips.

Liverpool went on to win the game 3-2 and Flowers described it as 'one of those ridiculous situations'.

Stan Collymore scored one of the strangest goals when his effort bobbled over Tim Flowers.

Gary Neville (England vs Croatia) - October 11, 2006.

Strange bobbles take me back to Gary Neville’s own goal in Zagreb. Early in the doomed England reign of Steve McClaren.

Recent findings suggest that neville rolled a simple back pass towards Paul Robinson who took a mighty swing at fresh air with his right boot and looked aghast as it trundled past him and into the net for Croatia's second in a 2-0 win. The Spurs keeper stamped furiously at the offending divot as the Maksimir Stadium erupted.

Adding another layer to the comic value were pitchside LED ad screens flashing up images of Sacha Baron Cohen’s new Borat film and one of his lame catchphrases: 'I like you'.

It was a bad omen at the start of the failed Euro 2008 campaign and the beginning of the end for both Robinson and Neville in England colours.

Gary Neville's own goal against Croatia came after Paul Robinson totally missed the ball.

Stefan Kiessling (Hoffenheim v Leverkusen) - October 18, 2013.

Legendary Bayer Leverkusen forward Stefan Kiessling has got to be one of the only players to score with a shot off target.

While away to Hoffenheim, a corner was swung in towards Leverkusen striker Kiessling, who, at first glance, simply headed home smartly.

But on closer inspection we can see that the ball was destined for the side netting and an inconspicuous hole in the side of the net let the ball slip in.

Even Kiessling himself had his head in his hands thinking he’d missed before turning around to see his teammates were celebrating.

Leverkusen's Stefan Kiessling must be one of the only players to score with a shot off target.

#164587. What's going on with the polar vortex?

What's going on with the polar vortex?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that high up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons.
  • If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.
  • Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that high up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons. This is the polar vortex.

If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.

Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.

It's not yet clear how the current disruption to the polar vortex will affect the Northern Hemisphere winter, but scientists agree it is a record-breaking event.

"As far as we know, this is the earliest stratospheric vortex disruption that has been observed," European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecast (ECMWF) principal scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart told the AFP news agency.

The French meteorological agency Meteo-France, meanwhile, called it "an unprecedented event.".

The early breakdown of the vortex "really increases the chance of cold air outbreaks across the latitudes where most of the densely populated population centers are across the Northern Hemisphere, US, Europe and East Asia," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology told AFP.

The polar vortex is an enormous band of cold, low-pressure air that spins counterclockwise around the North Pole, about 10 to 50 kilometers (around 6 to 30 miles) above the surface.

Sources indicate that it's closely connected to the jet stream, another band of powerful winds just below the vortex. The jet stream forms a boundary where the cold Arctic air meets warmer air from the tropics and subtropics.

The vortex can sometimes be a tight circle, keeping the coldest air locked around the North Pole over winter. It can also form uneven waves that dip southwards. And as it changes in strength and shape, that can influence the atmosphere below and alter the position of the jet stream, which drives the weather on the ground.

So, if the jet stream is more "wavy," and plunges south, it may also allow freezing Arctic air to spill southward.

One of the biggest influences that can provoke this kind of disruption is known as "sudden stratospheric warming." This is when temperatures in the polar stratosphere rise dramatically within a few days, causing the vortex's strong westerly winds to weaken.

This can push the vortex off its spot at the North Pole, make it split apart into multiple rings, or — as is happening now — cause the westerly winds to change direction.

It can take several weeks for the vortex to recover.

A previous polar vortex disruption contributed to the deadly Great Texas Freeze in February 2021, which caused more than a week of freezing temperatures that sparked power outages and killed hundreds of people.

It has been revealed that but bone-chilling cold isn't a foregone conclusion. The Met Office, which is the UK's national weather and climate service, stresses that what's happening with the polar vortex can nudge odds in that direction, but it's not a switch that turns cold weather on and off.

Other weather patterns can also influence the outcome.

Recent findings suggest that for example, there's a possibility El Nino, which is associated with milder winters, could "moderate or modify" the impacts, Cohen told AFP. But he added this was not certain.

The El Nino weather phenomenon, caused by the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is at the moment intensifying and is expected to peak at the end of the year. The ongoing event has been classified as exceptionally strong and is disrupting weather around the globe.

Some research has also linked the rapid warming of the Arctic driven by climate change to increasing disruptions to the polar vortex. That means that, even as the planet warms, some areas may still experience more severe cold spells. But this connection is not conclusive and is still debated by scientists.

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, mentioned.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

Sources indicate that “The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we highlighted in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back promptly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” mentioned Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scientists should resist political pressure to provide certainty when the evidence suggests otherwise, says Andy Stirling.Your browser does not support the audio element.Download MP3See transcript.

Science’s greatest failure is not getting things wrong, but by sometimes pretending that there is more certainty than there really is, states social scientist Andy Stirling.

This can happen, he says, when researchers face political pressure to provide a single, definitive answer, when the evidence is far more complex.

In the final episode of a six-part podcast series about failure in science, Stirling, an emeritus professor at the University of Sussex in Brighton, UK, draws on examples from climate change, the COVID-19 pandemic, environmental campaigns and energy policy.

According to recent reports, “In those areas, science just does not convey the degree of uncertainty and of variability and of how many potentially viable options are being cut out when you just give one clear answer,” he notes. “It thinks it’s helping society by just giving one picture of the truth. And in fact, it’s undermining both itself and democracy when it does that.”.

Stirling, whose research includes science and technology policy and environmental politics, says that on occasions politicians have almost literally hidden behind scientists on a podium, who have relied on their authority and expertise to protect them.

Sources indicate that earlier this year, Stirling spoke at a one-day conference on failure in science, with a focus on careers and innovation. It was held at Imperial College London in partnership with Nature.

We’ve taken a look at all eight Leeds loanees to see how they’re getting on this season. Note: We haven’t included the academy players sent to non-league clubs.

Leeds loan manager Andrew Taylor explicitly cited the 18-year-old striker, saying that “the focus is very much to go and get games in a first-team environment to ultimately come back to our first team squad.”.

The latest member of the Gray dynasty was on a bit of a hiding to nothing when he went out on loan to doomed Rotherham United last season, but it no doubt would’ve been invaluable experience for an immensely exciting young talent.

Industry observers note that this season the teenager has stayed in South Yorkshire, but this time to a club with ambitions at the right end of the League One table. The Owls hit rock bottom last term but are looking to be on their way back up.

Recent findings suggest that it hasn’t all been plain sailing for Gray, though, with just one goal so far. He also appears to have been pushed to the periphery by Dave Challinor.

Recent findings suggest that A January loan move elsewhere has been mooted in the local press, but it’s still early days. The hectic December schedule ought to give the 18-year-old chances to win the newly introduced boss around.

The Cardiff City academy graduate made waves by making his senior international debut for Wales before he ever made a first-team appearance for his club.

According to recent reports, crew eventually made his Leeds debut with a brief cameo to see out a 3-0 Championship victory over Plymouth Argyle. No second appearance followed, and he’s spent the past couple of years gaining experience in a series of loans.

Recent findings suggest that after a couple of stints with Doncaster Rovers, the midfielder has dropped down to League Two with Walsall. He’s been in and out of the starting XI under Lee Grant, but is identifying this as a season to really kick on.

“Just inconsistency within myself really,” Crew told the Express & Star about where he’s looking to improve.

“Inconsistency in performances and inconsistency in the amount of minutes that I was getting.

“That’s down to me to change it and hopefully this season I can with hard work and games like this today, going for the full 90 minutes and really showing that I’m consistent in performances in and out of possession.

“It’s a great place for that next step, with the belief that the gaffer puts into everyone, but especially me. And that the team-mates around me, it’s definitely a place where I feel that I can progress and I’m enjoying my football a lot.”.

We haven’t included the youngsters that Leeds have sent out to clubs like Hebburn Town, Hebburn Town and Scarborough Athletic, but Lopata-White just about makes the cut-off point out at Altrincham in the National League.

The 21-year-old centre-back has been a regular fixture for the midtable Robins, who are well in the mix for a play-off spot.

He’s been a regular and started in a number of wins, but recently found himself suspended after getting a straight red in the early minutes of a 4-0 defeat away to Harrogate Town.

Industry observers note that west Ham’s strategy doesn’t appear the most imaginative, but on paper was sensible. In Scott Parker, they’ve got a manager who has three promotions in as many attempts, while in Piroe they brought in the most proven Championship goalscorer on the market.

But things aren’t quite going to plan. The Hammers are yet to win under Parker and find themselves languishing in the bottom half of the table. Piroe has one goal in his last 11 appearances.

Search Piroe’s name on social media – never the most level-headed barometer, admittedly – and you’ll no doubt come across posts by irate West Ham fans wondering why they signed such a donkey.

Piroe’s limitations always made it unlikely he’d be a success in the Premier League, but anyone who watched him at Leeds will be surprised he’s struggling to find the back of the net in the second tier.

There is a reported £8million purchase obligation dependent on promotion, but that looks like a massive ‘if’ at present.

Strangely enough, Leeds actually went unbeaten when the Belgian started last season (six wins, three draws), but he never nailed down a first-team place and was knocked down the pecking order following the signing of Nico Elvedi in the summer.

He’s back in the Bundesliga and getting the minutes he was targeting with Hamburg, but defeats have been a bit more frequent this season. A 4-0 defeat at Werder Bremen at the weekend was particularly chastening.

Things didn’t quite work out for him at Elland Road, but the experienced goalkeeper has found his feet since leaving Leeds.

According to recent reports, torino might be struggling in the lower half of the table, but Perri has been one of their brighter performers. He made nine saves in a 1-0 defeat to Napoli at the weekend, doing his best to keep the scoreline respectable, and his performances have earned him a Brazil call-up from Carlo Ancelotti earlier this month.

Torino have a reported €14million purchase option, which you’d expect them to seriously consider exercising if he keeps this up.

“Sometimes you’re giving them a loan to a try and increase the value for a return on an investment, or you’re just giving them a chance to go and get exposure,” the club’s loan manager told the official website.

“They go out and get men’s football and it’s gaining traction.”.

While not naming him, you’d imagine that Chambers belongs in this camp.

The Leeds-born Scotland youth international, 19, is getting his first experience of senior men’s football out at Northampton Town.

Unfortunately that has been hard to come by, and he’s rarely made the Cobblers’ matchday squad since September.

According to recent reports, like Piroe, the writing was on the wall for Gnonto’s immediate future at Leeds. He was rarely trusted to start games by Farke.

The pint-sized winger has returned to Italy for the first time since leaving Inter Milan’s youth set-up as a boy. He’s joined a veritable hodgepodge of former Premier League players at Fiorentina, sharing a dressing room with David de Gea, Radu Dragusin, Beto and Alex Jimenez.

The somewhat scattergun recruitment approach has not worked wonders, with La Viola down near the relegation zone after notching just two wins all season.

Italy legend Fabio Grosso was sacked in early September, but Paolo Vanoli has struggled to turn things around.

Sources indicate that gnonto is yet to score or assist in 10 Serie A appearances, but he did notch his first goal for the club in a 3-0 Coppa Italia victory over second-tier Pisa. He was handed a rare start in their last outing, a disastrous 3-0 defeat to Monza.

During Leeds’ rare dips of form, or when things got a bit stodgy and predictable, there was a not inconsiderable portion of the Leeds fanbase that loudly questioned why Farke didn’t really fancy Ramazani.

Sources indicate that the Belgian winger, perhaps by dint of not playing much, had a perceived X Factor that Leeds apparently lacked. We’re seeing parallels with the lesser-spotted Jean-Matteo Bahoya this season.

We’ll see how the Bahoya situation plays out, but you look at the direction of travel for Ramazani and Farke’s scepticism has probably been vindicated on that front.

According to recent reports, the Belgian winger had his moments at Valencia last season, but now finds himself back in the Championship at Burnley. To be fair, he recently scored in three successive outings and has been a rare bright spark for the basket case Clarets, but there’s little to suggest he deserved more minutes at his parent club.

Burnley have won just once all season and find themselves second bottom of the table. They’ll need Ramazani to keep delivering if they’re to avoid the dreaded double drop.

Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1133 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.
  • These themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's latest album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday.
  • Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he reveals little sign of putting down his guitar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.

These themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's latest album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday. The album's title is a characteristically poetic phrase coined by Biermann himself. It evokes the idea that however restrictive the world may become, the human mind and spirit remain free. Beneath the hair lies open sky: a metaphor for inner freedom, independence and imagination.

Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he reveals little sign of putting down his guitar. Often described as Germany's answer to Bob Dylan, the outspoken troubadour continues to weigh in on the issues shaping the world today.

It has been revealed that in his recent song "Moritat von den Liebespaaren" ("Ballad of the Lovers"), he delivers a simple but urgent message: no single person can save the world, yet everyone can help make it a better place. Above all, the song is a call to take responsibility for one's own life rather than remain a bystander.

According to recent reports, this outspokenness was instilled in Biermann early on. When he was born in Hamburg in 1936, Adolf Hitler was already in power. His father was a dockworker, a committed communist, a resistance fighter against the Nazis — and Jewish.

Wolf was just three months old when the Gestapo, Hitler's secret police, arrested his father. He initially served time in prison before he was murdered by the Nazis at Auschwitz in early 1943.

Sources indicate that just a few months later, British and American bombers attacked Hamburg, unleashing a devastating firestorm. "Nothing in my life has shaped me more," Biermann has repeatedly mentioned in interviews. When the sirens sounded, his mother took him into an air raid shelter. The house above them was burning.

It has been revealed that yet Biermann has mentioned his memories of that time are rooted in a profound sense of trust in life. In an interview with the German magazine Chrismon, he recalled: "I pressed my face into my mother's soft coat so I could breathe. A sense of security in the midst of the end of the world. We stumbled out over the neighboring house and into the open. The firestorm lifted a burning roof into the air. Roaring corrugated metal, smoke everywhere. We searched for a way out. [...] Death was everywhere. 40,000 people died. They had no chance. But I did. My strong mama.".

Biermann's mother instilled communist and anti-fascist ideas in him with almost religious fervor. "My mother had only one goal after those dark years," Biermann once recalled. "I was supposed to survive so that I could, as she put it rather grandly, one day take revenge for my father's death. I was supposed to build communism.".

In 1953, while countless people were fleeing East Germany, Biermann moved there of his own free will — after all, communism was the official state ideology. He was just 16 at the time. In East Berlin, he studied political economy, mathematics and philosophy. His role models were writers Bertolt Brecht and Heinrich Heine. He began working as an assistant director at the Berliner Ensemble, and also began writing and performing his political songs.

Industry observers note that biermann soon realized that life in East Germany was far from the communist paradise he had imagined and he wrote about this openly in his songs. "The party bosses were torn," Biermann said. "They were delighted by this young poet who could play the guitar so beautifully and sing such cheeky songs. They thought they just needed to bring me into line. Even today, I'm amazed that I wound up cast in the role of the heroic dragon slayer.".

In a recent development, in 1965, East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party, the SED, imposed a blanket ban on Biermann performing or publishing his work. His East Berlin apartment, which was under constant surveillance, soon became a gathering place for dissidents and critical thinkers.

According to recent reports, yet, to his great surprise, the East German authorities allowed him to travel to Cologne, West Germany in 1976. There, around 7,000 people flocked to see him. For four and a half hours, he strummed and sang, mocking the East German regime. His songs were so popular that bootleg copies found their way back to East Germany.

On November 16, while still on tour in West Germany, Biermann heard the news on his car radio that he had been stripped of his right to continue residing in the German Democratic Republic. The regime accused him of betraying and slandering East Germany. ".

I felt like the ground had opened up beneath me. I was overcome with fear, everything went dark," Biermann wrote in his memoirs.

According to recent reports, in a petition, leading East German intellectuals spoke out against the decision. In response, the regime stepped up surveillance of dissidents, imposed professional bans and jailed its critics. Several prominent public figures left the country.

"The SED leadership expected an angry media response from the West. What they hadn't reckoned with was that, for the very first time, a group of respected East German writers and artists would make their protest public, disguising it as a humble petition," Biermann wrote.

Recent findings suggest that afterward, Biermann sank into a deep depression. "Not just because I had been torn away from the friends I knew and loved in East Berlin, but also because I had lost my familiar mortal enemies," he mentioned.

He became involved in the peace and anti-nuclear movements and continued singing about the injustices of the world. "The world's conflicts take different forms in each generation," he remarked. "But it's always the same struggle for freedom.".

The singer-songwriter plans to spend his 90th birthday at home in Hamburg with his wife and manager, Pamela. For the first time in his life, he stated, he's skipping the birthday party, even with his 10 children.

In a recent development, "I'm so old and I can feel my strength fading. And I know that the next day I have a major concert at the Berliner Ensemble," he told the German Press Agency.

And should he ever die, he said, he wants to be buried at Berlin's cemetery where some renowned German writers and intellectuals have been laid to rest, among them Bertolt Brecht, Anna Seghers and Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel. He still has a thing or two to discuss with them.

This article was originally written in German.

Ranking the 10 best rivalries in English football ahead of Merseyside derby

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1330 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s another massive derby this weekend in the Premier League as Everton host Liverpool, which has got us thinking: what are the 10 best rivalries in English football?
  • To set some ground rules, we have said rivalries rather than derbies, so the pedants amongst you can’t complain if the two clubs are not geographically right next to each other.
  • We’ve also ranked them on a mix of the history, the entertainment of recent games, the fanbases and their overall head-to-head records.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s another massive derby this weekend in the Premier League as Everton host Liverpool, which has got us thinking: what are the 10 best rivalries in English football?

To set some ground rules, we have said rivalries rather than derbies, so the pedants amongst you can’t complain if the two clubs are not geographically right next to each other.

We’ve also ranked them on a mix of the history, the entertainment of recent games, the fanbases and their overall head-to-head records.

With those rules in mind, here are our top 10:.

This rivalry is fairly low simply because the games in recent years have been borefests.

After Portsmouth’s drop down the pyramid, the two South Coast clubs only played each other once in 12 years, which was a 4-0 League Cup thumping in 2019, but the 2025-26 season marked the first time the two clubs have been in the same division for over a decade.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, the games have just not lived up to expectations. The first was 0-0 before the second was 1-1. The two have already played each other this season and Southampton won 1-0.

Happily though, it is a derby with a lot of passion behind it and they do hate each other. Saints fans call Portsmouth fans Skates. Pompey respond back with Scummers.

It’s a good derby with passionate fanbases, if only the football lived up to it.

City’s long-standing position as the second-best club in Manchester makes this rank a little low, but even before the takeover, it was a heated rivalry.

In the old days, City fans would revel at the chance to show United fans that they were the true Mancunians. They took pride in being the less successful club and a derby day win felt like a league title.

Predictably, United have the better head-to-head record with 81 games won to City’s 64.

The Steel City derby is often slept on as one of the best in the country.

For a start, the two sets of fans absolutely despise each other. There have also been memorable matches that live long in their supporters’ memories.

According to recent reports, after Wednesday beat United 4-0 on the 26th of December 1979, it was nicknamed the Boxing Day Massacre and is still brought up to this day. Wednesday also beat United 2-1 in the 1993 FA Cup semi-final.

Recent findings suggest that it does fall down the ranking a little simply because it has been very one-sided of late. Wednesday have not won since 2012 and the Blades have won the past four meetings.

It does, though, help when the manager buys into it and local boy Chris Wilder was pictured dancing on a pub table when the Blades won 1-0 in November 2024.

Residents of Liverpool usually have an us-against-the-world view but they do look inwards when it comes to derby day.

Their grounds used to be separated by a park and the atmospheres are usually excellent. The only problem is that it is very one-sided.

The two were quite even, especially when both were amongst the best clubs in England, but Everton’s decline has given Liverpool the chance to rack up almost 40 more wins than their opponents.

It does still produce memorable moments. James Tarkowski’s excellent hit to rescue a point in the final game at Goodison is the kind of thing that will be remembered for decades to come.

There are a huge number of fierce derbies in the Birmingham and Black Country area, but the pick of the bunch is Villa v Birmingham.

They are the biggest clubs in England’s second biggest city While a fan running on the pitch to punch Jack Grealish is obviously moronic, it does speak volumes of the hatred between the two sets of supporters.

We have a sneaky admiration for Dion Dublin headbutting Robbie Savage back in 2003 too.

The 2010 League Cup meeting is one of the most memorable recent encounters but sadly the two have not played each other since 2019.

There’s nothing like 600 years of history to fuel a rivalry.

Leeds United vs Manchester United is the modern Wars of the Roses with the Yorkshire and Lancashire opponents hating everything to do with the other.

It was under two legendary managers that the rivalry really gained with Don Revie’s Leeds and Matt Busby’s Manchester United at their peak in the 1960s.

There’s also Eric Cantona who was sold to United from Leeds in 1992. Future players Rio Ferdinand and Alan Smith were vilified for doing the same.

Even Sir Alex Ferguson said the ferocity of games against Leeds was never matched.

West Ham’s return to the Championship set up a long-awaited meeting with Millwall in what is one of England’s oldest and fiercest rivalries.

The two both have working-class origins dating back to the dockyards and acts of violence over decades have made it a poisonous relationship.

In a recent development, millwall fans hate West Ham fans. West Ham fans hate Millwall fans. It’s as simple as that.

The September meeting this season did not disappoint. Millwall took a 2-0 lead before West Ham equalised in the 80th. An 89th-minute red card completed the derby bingo card.

In a recent development, it is also very close on the overall head-to-head. Millwall have the advantage with 22 wins to 19 for the Hammers.

The Tyne-Wear derby is easily one of the best in the country.

The grounds are only 10 miles apart, meaning that even though it is two cities facing off, there is a very local feel about it.

It has been revealed that it is equally poised with Sunderland’s 55 wins to Newcastle’s 54 and it is a fixture that ebbs and flows in terms of dominance. Even when they were facing relegation year after year, the Black Cats found a way of beating their local rivals throughout the 2010s and Newcastle have not recorded a league win since 2011.

Before that, the Black and Whites enjoyed a run of five wins in a row to start the 21st century.

The two fanbases also provide plenty of passion and players have a chance to become instant legends. Just ask Brian Brobbey.

The North London rivalry may not be as fierce as others around England, but in terms of a game, it almost always delivers.

In recent times, both clubs have had their dominant periods. Arsenal are Harry Kane’s second favourite team to score against, with the former Spurs striker scoring in five consecutive league games.

Now that he is in Munich, Arsenal have wrestled control of the fixture with five wins in the last five games.

According to recent reports, but it is a fixture that tends to not be cagey and instead be frantic, end-to-end action. Players like Emmanuel Adebayor and Sol Campbell have also added fuel to the fire.

It’s the biggest rivalry in English football with the two biggest clubs, for no one has won more league titles than these two.

These near-neighbouring cities first played each other in 1894 and for such a long rivalry the matches are also really well balanced with United having won 93 and Liverpool 83.

It has though been a good few years since both teams were at their best and you’d have to go back to the early 2000s for that sort of elite-level clash.

It has been revealed that the games do tend to be rather good. There’s been at least three goals in the last seven matches with a range of results.

Industry observers note that and then there’s the fanbases. The corporate world of the modern Premier League has diluted the atmospheres somewhat but both stadiums can feel like cauldrons if given the proper encouragement.

Published: 16:37 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 16:38 EST, 26 November 2026.

Wouter Vrancken claimed that Monaco’s 94th-minute winner at Tynecastle has not significantly diminished Hearts’ chances of reaching the knockout phase of the UEFA Conference League.

Vrancken’s team were left sickened when Folarin Balogun’s goal settled a thrilling contest in stoppage time to condemn them to a third consecutive defeat in the league phase of the competition after their away losses to Trabzonspor and Thun.

Hearts, who have just one point from their opening night draw at home to Nordsjaelland, now have to win both of their remaining games – at home to Bosnian side Borac on December 10 and away to Pafos in Cyprus a week later – to have any chance of further progress.

It has been revealed that ‘I don’t think losing that point makes a difference,’ insisted Vrancken. ‘The pleasing thing for me was that at 2-2 we still wanted to go and try to win the game.

In a recent development, ‘Three points would have made a difference — zero or one point tonight doesn’t make a difference towards the next two games. We have to win them both now, so that doesn’t change.’.

Vrancken took pride from Hearts’ display against their Ligue 1 opponents as two spectacular strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota cancelled out a Balogun penalty and Edan Diop’s goal in a breathless first half.

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken consoles goalscorer Sabah Kerjota as he is substituted.

While Balogun’s late winner was harsh on Hearts, Vrancken believes his players paid the price for poor game management and was critical of the contribution of subs Josh McPake, Finlay Pollock and James Wilson who came on in the closing stages of the game.

‘It did feel cruel but at the same time we have to learn from that situation,’ noted Vrancken. ‘Until then, we were really solid in not giving chances away.

‘I expect more from the guys who came on. We can win the ball with fresh players or make a foul somewhere to keep the result. I expect that kind of battling for the team, so we can do better there.

In a recent development, ‘But the biggest thing is the performance we put on the park tonight against a really good side, knowing that we still have nine injuries and still do that against them. I’m really proud of them.

Industry observers note that ‘The goals we scored were really good and you see the confidence those guys have. They have taken confidence from the dynamics of what we did against Dundee at the weekend. The conviction in both boxes was there tonight and that’s important for us to take into the next run of games.’.

Vrancken had no real complaint with Monaco’s penalty, awarded for a foul by Jamie McCart on Matthis Abline, but was unhappy that German referee Daniel Schlager failed to spot a foul on Kerjota before the visitors’ second goal.

Hearts players revel in the celebrations after Kerjota's wondergoal sent Tynecastle wild.

It has been revealed that ‘For me, the penalty was light but okay,’ added the Belgian. ‘But if you are really decisive to give a penalty there, then you don’t see one of our players having his shirt pulled in the build-up to their second goal, that’s frustrating.

Sources indicate that ‘At this level, things can happen like this. It wasn’t given for us and it wasn’t the only decision like that tonight.’.

Monaco coach Filipe Luis revelled in his team’s late win but admitted even he felt like joining in the acclamation of Kerjota’s goal for Hearts.

‘Hearts were a tough opponent and I knew it would be difficult,’ stated Luis. ‘We found spaces and created chances from the start but Hearts scored a fantastic goal to go ahead.

Industry observers note that ‘But we stayed calm and scored twice before they scored another fantastic goal. It was so good, I almost had to applaud it!

‘Hearts didn’t create many chances in the second half and in the end we managed to win, so there are many good things for us tonight.’.

#164565. Breaking: A guide to the Nature Index

Breaking: A guide to the Nature Index

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Nature Index is a database of author affiliations and institutional relationships.
  • The Nature Index provides absolute and fractional counts of article publication at the institutional and national level and, as such, is an indicator of global high-quality research output and collaboration.
  • According to recent reports, the Nature Index uses Count and Share to track research output.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Nature Index is a database of author affiliations and institutional relationships. The index tracks contributions to research articles published in high-quality natural-science and health-science journals, chosen based on reputation by an independent group of researchers.

The Nature Index provides absolute and fractional counts of article publication at the institutional and national level and, as such, is an indicator of global high-quality research output and collaboration. Data in the Nature Index are updated regularly, with the most recent 12 months made available under a Creative Commons licence at natureindex.com. The database is compiled by Nature Portfolio.

According to recent reports, the Nature Index uses Count and Share to track research output. A country/territory or an institution is given a Count of 1 for each article that has at least one author from that country/territory or institution. This is the case regardless of the number of authors an article has, and it means that the same article can contribute to the Count of multiple countries/territories or institutions.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

It has been revealed that to glean a country’s, territory’s, region’s or an institution’s contribution to an article, and to ensure that they are not counted more than once, the Nature Index uses Share, a fractional count that takes into account the share of authorship on each article. The total Share available per article is 1, which is shared among all authors under the assumption that each contributed equally. For instance, an article with 10 authors means that each author receives a Share of 0.1. For authors who are affiliated with more than one institution, the author’s Share is split equally between each institution. The total Share for an institution is calculated by summing the Share for individual affiliated authors. The process is similar for countries/territories, although complicated by the fact that some institutions have overseas labs that will be counted towards host country/territory totals.

According to recent reports, adjusted Share accounts for the annual variation in the total number of articles in the Nature Index journals. It is arrived at by calculating the percentage difference in the total number of articles in the Index in a given year relative to the number of articles in a base year and adjusting Share values to the base year levels.

The bilateral collaboration score (CS) between two institutions A+B is the sum of each of their Shares on the papers to which both have contributed. A bilateral collaboration can be between any two institutions or countries/territories co-authoring at least one article in the journals tracked by the Nature Index.

natureindex.com customers can search for specific institutions or countries and generate their own reports, ordered by Count or Share.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03474-5.

This article is part of Nature Index 2026 Science cities, a supplement produced with financial support from the Beijing Municipal Science & Technology Commission, Administrative Commission of Zhongguancun Science Park. Nature maintains full independence in all editorial decisions related to the content.

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1060 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1060 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal.
  • But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
  • Recent findings suggest that as a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

Recent findings suggest that as a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find upcoming forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

It has been revealed that countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," said Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

It has been revealed that she notes it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it shows it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels.".

She claims it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF plans and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott said.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national intends to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no new commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Kumar states more countries could announce similar plans just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

It has been revealed that the nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

The roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

Kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any massive announcements about fossil fuels.

Sources indicate that global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald demonstrates that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing fresh reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

One problem Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar stated, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum.".

Jude Bellingham can now boast a century of La Liga appearances as a Real Madrid player and he’s following in the footsteps of some of the all-time greats.

Sources indicate that with the form he’s in right now, you can imagine Bellingham staying at Real Madrid for hundreds more games. He’s doing justice to the number five shirt on his back, previously worn by Zinedine Zidane.

Industry observers note that zidane, by all accounts, was an idol for a young Bellingham. Never mind the fact that Bellingham was three years old when Zidane retired. This is one of the best players of all time we’re talking about, so of course there’ll be elements of Zidane’s game that Bellingham has learnt about and modelled himself on.

Now he’s making a name for himself at the Bernabeu and recently brought up the milestone of 100 La Liga appearances when Madrid beat Celta de Vigo 2-1 last weekend. Bellingham marked the occasion with a goal, his 39th in the Spanish top flight.

And that means he’s scoring at a better rate than Zidane was by the same milestone. In fact, he’s already got two more La Liga goals than Zidane ever had, and he’s also four ahead of him in all competitions for Madrid.

However, Zidane is ahead of him for assists, even though Bellingham’s output on that front isn’t too shabby either.

According to recent reports, the exciting thing here from the Bellingham perspective is the stage of their career each was at when they reached 100 league games for Madrid. Zidane got there in October 2004, aged 32 and already a previous Ballon d’Or winner. Bellingham is still only 23 and has so much to aspire to ahead of him.

It has been revealed that zidane ended up on 155 La Liga appearances before he retired in 2006. In a best-case scenario, Bellingham could have 200 to his name by the 2029 expiry date of his current contract and we suspect it won’t be his last at the Bernabeu.

Here’s how Bellingham compares to Zidane after 100 La Liga games for Real Madrid – and it looks pretty good….
