It has been revealed that so much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Recent findings suggest that jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

Sources indicate that in between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX.

It has been revealed that A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

Industry observers note that "Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ.

According to recent reports, tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. It has been revealed that tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

According to recent reports, tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest game in South American club football takes place this weekend with the 2026 edition of the Copa Libertadores final.

Palmeiras will take on Estudiantes at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo on Saturday, but which faces might you recognise?

Here are seven of the players in the two squads who featured in the Premier League at some point.

Everton fans will remember Funes Mori, who was at Goodison from 2015 to 2018.

He signed for £9.5m and played a decent amount in the 2015-16 season with Phil Jagielka and John Stones regularly out with injuries.

A red card in the Merseyside derby relegated him back to the bench and he ended the following season by tearing his meniscus with Argentina.

It took until April of the following season for him to return to the squad but he was shipped out in the summer to Villarreal.

His path to Estudiantes has gone from Villarreal to Al Nassr to Cruz Azul to River Plate and then finally at his current club who he joined last year.

Lisandro Martinez may be Man Utd’s current underperforming Argentine centre-back but before him it was Marcos Rojo filling that role.

He was signed under Louis van Gaal who actually managed to get some decent performances out of him early on and he was at United for a surprisingly long time, staying into 2021 although he did not play more than 10 league games for the final four seasons.

After his United career came to an end, he moved back to Argentina to join Boca Juniors before joining Racing Club in 2025.

He left them in August before signing with Estudiantes, his former club, in 2026.

The Belgian-born Brazilian started his career at Manchester United as a member of their youth academy but struggled for game time and was loaned out to four different teams.

He found more of a home in West London, joining Fulham in 2022 and making 119 appearances for the club.

He joined Palmeiras in 2025 and was played in the 2025 Copa Libertadores final, losing 1-0 against his former club Flamengo.

In between two separate stints at Lazio, Brazilian winger Anderson joined West Ham.

West Ham being West Ham means they signed him for a club-record fee of £36m but they did not get much return on their investment.

His first season was okay with nine goals in 36 Premier League matches but that shrank to one in 25 for his second.

That level of performance saw him go out on loan to Porto before moving back to Lazio ahead of the 2021/22 season.

He left Europe in 2024, moving to Palmeiras where he is still playing at the age of 33.

14 forgotten ballers now playing in Brazil as Seedorf becomes Lingard’s manager.

Recent findings suggest that after Wolves fans had to watch Matheus Cunha go to Manchester United, the club tried to soften the blow by giving his number 10 shirt to upcoming signing Jhon Arias. It didn’t go well.

The Colombian joined for £15m and played 26 times for the club but scored just two goals as they went down.

Arias was not there to see it through though as he left for Palmeiras in February.

If the pointless question was to name the most obscure Southampton player from the 2010s, then Guido Carrillo is your man.

The striker joined the St Mary’s club in the 2018 winter transfer window for a fee of £19m but would make just 10 appearances in his two years at the club.

He spent the latter of those on loan at Leganes who he joined the summer after he signed for Southampton with the Premier League club clearly feeling they had made a mistake.

In October 2020, his contract was terminated and he joined Elche before moving to the excellently named Henan Songshan Longmen and arriving at Estudiantes in 2023.

It was a blink-and-you-miss-it Premier League period for Sosa who spent a single year in the Premier League before disappearing back to South America.

The Paraguayan had never played European football before making the move to the City Ground for £9.3m.

Sources indicate that the left winger signed a five-year deal and even managed to score in his second game but barely featured throughout the season. On just one occasion did he play more than an hour for the club as Nuno Espirito Santo clearly didn’t fancy him.

Despite this, Forest somehow made a profit with him moving to Palmeiras for £10m.

What would the Premier League table look like if Man City get kicked out?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Some reports suggest City’s Premier League rivals are keen for any punishment to be dished out before the end of the current campaign and while that could be anything from a fine to a transfer ban to a points deduction, it is not out of the realm of possibility that City are kicked out of the league entirely.
  • Sources indicate that expulsion from a league is not without precedent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While Manchester City’s future is up in the air, one real possibility is that they could be expelled from the Premier League this season.

Some reports suggest City’s Premier League rivals are keen for any punishment to be dished out before the end of the current campaign and while that could be anything from a fine to a transfer ban to a points deduction, it is not out of the realm of possibility that City are kicked out of the league entirely.

Sources indicate that expulsion from a league is not without precedent. Both Bury and Maidstone United were kicked out of the Football League due to financial reasons but, crucially, had not played a match that season.

It would, though, be unheard of in Premier League history and would have a knock-on effect for all other 19 clubs, not to mention the ones who have already played City.

In a recent development, if City are expelled during the season, the most likely outcome is that their results would be expunged from the record. How different would that make the current Premier League table look?

If City were expelled during the season, Premier League Rule C.15 states that their results would be expunged from the league table and the number of relegation places reduced by one. However, if they were expelled after the season had concluded, C.15 would not apply in the same way, meaning their completed results would not automatically be wiped from the table.

City had won their first seven Premier League games, meaning none of their rivals would have lost any points from the hypothetical expulsion.

In a recent development, but three losses and a home draw against Fulham change things slightly. They’d be the only teams to lose points in our table.

The obvious place to start then is that every team except Arsenal and Brighton would move up one spot due to City at the moment being third in the table.

That would put Arsenal top with 28 points from 11 matches, eight clear of Brighton in second. Liverpool would be third, albeit with a game in hand on the Gunners.

At the other end, Sunderland, Manchester United and Crystal Palace would occupy the bottom three, although the reduction in relegation places would mean only United and Palace would be going down.

Sources indicate that as for the goals, Sunderland would be happy to see five wiped off their conceded tally although would lose three of their own. Liverpool and Ipswich would see three goals wiped off too.

It would be win-win for United and Coventry who would have one taken off their conceded without anything happening to their scored column.

Bournemouth and Palace both scored one in their defeats to City so would also be up overall in terms of goal difference.

Brighton would boast the best goal difference in the division at +16, having scored an impressive 25 goals in their 10 matches against the other 18 clubs.

Here’s how the 2026-27 table shapes up if you expunge City’s results from the record.

Hearts 2-3 Monaco: Late agony for brave hosts in Conference League tie - as Folarin Balogun strikes at the death to settle rollercoaster Tynecastle epic

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:54 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 17:41 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • On a pulsating but ultimately painful evening for Hearts, their bid to reach the knockout phase of the UEFA Conference League suffered an agonising 94th-minute blow after they had gone toe-to-toe with a classy Monaco side.
  • USA World Cup striker Folarin Balogun’s stoppage-time winner preserved the Ligue 1 club’s perfect record in the league stage of the tournament and leaves Wouter Vrancken’s men with no remaining room for error.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:54 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 17:41 EST, 26 November 2026.

On a pulsating but ultimately painful evening for Hearts, their bid to reach the knockout phase of the UEFA Conference League suffered an agonising 94th-minute blow after they had gone toe-to-toe with a classy Monaco side.

USA World Cup striker Folarin Balogun’s stoppage-time winner preserved the Ligue 1 club’s perfect record in the league stage of the tournament and leaves Wouter Vrancken’s men with no remaining room for error.

Hearts must now win their last two games next month, at home to Bosnian side Borac and away to Pafos in Cyprus, to finish on seven points which could still be enough to secure a top 24 place in the 36-team standings.

It was a sickening conclusion to a thrilling match which saw Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota both score goal-of-the-season contenders for Hearts in a rollercoaster first half in which Balogun and Edan Diop were on target for Monaco.

Hearts emerged from the night with plenty of credit for their bold and often enterprising approach but it is points rather than plaudits they now need if their European campaign is to carry on beyond Christmas.

This would have been a challenging assignment for Hearts under any circumstances but the degree of difficulty was increased for Vrancken’s side by their injury list.

USA striker Folarin Balogun celebrates the late goal that broke hearts at Tynecastle.

While easing slightly in recent weeks, with Blair Spittal the latest welcome returnee as he took a place on the bench, it remains significant and the Hearts coach was only able to name six outfield players among his subs.

With winger Josh McPake a surprising omission from the starting line-up, Vrancken sought greater solidity with the inclusion of 19-year-old defensive midfielder Matty Gillies.

After two sub outings since being recalled from his loan at Stenhousemuir, it was a baptism of fire for the teenager as he made his first start for Hearts.

Along with his more experienced team-mates, Gillies was chasing shadows for the opening ten minutes or so as Monaco moved the ball around with pace, precision and real intent.

Matthis Abline was a real thorn in the side of the Hearts defence and there was an early warning sign when the striker cut them open and teed up a good chance for Takumi Minamino. The former Liverpool winger couldn’t get his shot away, instead scuffing the ball into the path of Diop whose effort was blocked.

It was looking ominous for Hearts at this stage, with Abline quickly surging clear again to set up Christian Mawissa for a shot which flew well over the top, but they gradually secured a foothold in the contest.

Monaco forward Balogun sends the ball beyond Beau Reus to settle a rollercoaster match.

Pierre Landry Kabore was first to threaten for the hosts when he muscled his way into the Monaco penalty area but the big striker’s lack of finesse and awareness saw him drag a shot wide when he should have picked out Gillies in a more promising position.

Sources indicate that hearts grew in belief and made the 16th-minute breakthrough with their first wonder strike of the evening. Kerjota’s free-kick from around 20 yards was a decent enough hit, the ball rebounding off Lukas Hradecky’s left hand post.

Recent findings suggest that claudio Braga did well to keep possession for Hearts and found Altena on the edge of the box. The Dutch full-back displayed outstanding technique to smash a rising shot beyond the helpless Hradecky and send the home fans into raptures.

Monaco briefly appeared rattled and Hearts might have done more to take advantage of a mix-up between Hradecky and Sadibou Sane which saw Laurent Mendy nick the ball and find Kabore who again lacked the composure needed to get a shot on target.

Just as it seemed Hearts were in the ascendancy, however, they gifted Monaco an equaliser. It was another unhappy moment in Europe for Jamie McCart, who scored an own goal in Hearts’ previous game away to Swiss side Thun.

The defender caught Abline with a rash and clumsy challenge inside the box, leaving German referee Daniel Schlager with a simple decision to make as he pointed to the spot.

Jordi Altena turns to celebrate his exquisite opener that sent the Tynecastle crowd wild.

Balogun stepped forward and calmly slotted the penalty low to the left of Beau Reus and into the corner of the net.

The goal sparked another spell of dominance from the visitors who were finding it all too easy to pass their way through central midfield where Gillies and Laurent Mendy were regularly outnumbered.

Balogun came close to finding the net again when he got in behind McCart on the left side of the penalty area before dragging a shot just wide from a difficult angle.

The visitors did take the lead in the 41st minute and, once more, Hearts were the architects of their own downfall. This time, they conceded possession cheaply from their own throw-in when Altena took one touch too many and gave the ball away.

Monaco ruthlessly made the most of the opening it presented as Balogun raced clear and set up the unmarked Diop for a simple close-range finish.

No sooner had they seized the initiative, however, Monaco found themselves back on level terms once again as Kerjota conjured up a stunning goal which was arguably even better than Altena’s opener.

Sabah Kerjota unleashes a ridiculous left-footed shot that sailed gracefully into the top corner.

Recent findings suggest that sabri Guendouz, whose pace and direct running was a real headache for Monaco, did well to earn a free-kick on the left. Altena flighted it to the far post where Stuart Findlay won the aerial battle. The ball fell to Kerjota on the right corner of the penalty area and he curled a sumptuous shot beyond Hradecky into the top left corner of the net.

A remarkable first half almost ended with a third Hearts goal in stoppage time. Minamino, already booked, was fortunate to avoid a second yellow card when he tripped Guendouz on the edge of the box. Altena’s set piece expertise was called upon again and he was unlucky to see his dipping effort narrowly clear the crossbar.

Hearts had to defend smartly and bravely for long spells in the second half, no one doing it better than McCart who recovered brilliantly from his earlier setback as he produced several crucial interventions.

Reus had to make fine saves to deny Jordan Teze and Abline but Hearts had menacing moments of their own. Hopes were raised when the ref pointed to the spot for handball against Monaco sub Mathys Detourbet in the 71st minute but the award was rightly reversed by VAR.

Albanian winger Kerjota takes the acclaim of his team-mates before the late heartbreak.

Rogers Mato made an astonishing goal-line clearance to prevent Detourbet scoring at the other end and it looked as if Hearts would hold on for a valuable point.

Then came the late, late heartbreak as Mamadou Coulibaly sent Balogun racing free to coolly slot the ball beyond Reus and leave Hearts’ prospects of further progress in the tournament hanging by a thread.

Sources indicate that hearts (4-2-3-1): Reus 7; Altena 7, McCart 7, Findlay 7, Borchgrevink 6 (Mato 46); Gillies 5 (Spittal 46), Mendy 6; Kerjota 8 (Pollock 81), Braga 6 (Wilson 85), Guendouz 7 (McPake 76); Kabore 6. Booked: Altena, Kabore. Manager: Wouter Vrancken 7.

Sources indicate that monaco (3-4-2-1): Hradecky 7; Sane 7, Dier 7, Teze 7; Vanderson 6 (Nazinho 57), Zakaria 6, Diop 6 (Coulibaly 64), Mawissa 6 (Detourbet 64); Minamino 6 (Belmokhtar 57), Abline 8 (Soubeir 87); Balogun 8. Booked: Abline, Minamino, Mawissa, Detourbet. Manager: Filipe Luis 7.

Referee: Daniel Schlager (Germany).

#164555. The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

📅 28 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1315 w)

The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1315 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty.
  • Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment.
  • A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment. Twice-yearly injections of this game-changing medicine — originally developed by the firm Gilead Sciences in Foster City, California — have been shown to be more than 95% effective at preventing HIV acquisition1. At the same time, as Nature reports in a News feature, an HIV vaccine — that would ultimately be a more robust solution to preventing HIV — is closer than ever before.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

In 2024, Gilead signed licensing agreements with six pharmaceutical companies, allowing them to make and sell generic versions of lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries, subject to regulatory approval. The recent FDA approval brings access a step closer in these countries. The cost to users has been set at US$40 per year, fuelling hopes that the drug will help to bring the global HIV epidemic under control.

In a recent development, these welcome developments contrast with the situation of public funding for HIV research and treatment, which is reeling from deep and unconscionable cuts from the US government. Many of the researchers whom Nature spoke to for the News feature had been funded by a programme for preclinical HIV-vaccine research run by the US National Institutes of Health (NIH). But the agency ended the programme last year, forcing researchers to scale back their research and seek alternative funding. Whatever funding comes next is likely to be less stable and less predictable than the NIH funding. It’s imperative that the cuts be reversed — or upcoming government funding sources found.

The path to an HIV vaccine has been long and bumpy, with decades of high-profile and costly failures, but there is now light at the end of the tunnel. The latest strategy — known as germline targeting — is designed to trigger the production of rare, highly potent antibodies that can prevent infection with diverse HIV strains. The technique has shown encouraging results in animal models2–4 and in early trials in humans5. Researchers are more optimistic than they’ve been in years that an effective HIV vaccine could be on the horizon.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

But in the meantime, antiretroviral drugs such as lenacapavir look poised to have a major impact on infection prevention. In Africa alone, upcoming infections could be cut by around one-third if just 5% of adults most likely to acquire HIV received the drug, and by half if it was given to one-fifth of adults, according to the Gates Foundation’s Institute for Disease Modelling in Seattle, Washington.

According to recent reports, but lenacapavir alone is unlikely to bring the HIV epidemic fully under control. There are several reasons for this: first, it’s not always easy to determine who needs the drug most. Second, to be effective, the drug must be taken for most of someone’s life — or at least while they are sexually active. Third, even $40 a year is unaffordable for people on the very lowest incomes.

Sources indicate that until recently, the United States was the stand-out funder for antiretroviral drugs for people living with HIV in low-and middle-income countries. That stopped in January 2025, when the US administration suspended funding. Although it later restored a limited amount, the effects have been devastating. A survey published earlier this year found that some 1,700 facilities previously offering treatments to people living with HIV had closed as a result (see go.nature.com/4a7ftp4).

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Sources indicate that such instability highlights the importance of vaccines. “The funding cuts that happened in the past couple of years have really made it even more obvious how fragile that system of reliance” on drug access is, indicates Penny Moore, a virologist at South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Disease in Johannesburg. And that fragility, as Rogier Sanders, an HIV-vaccine researcher at Amsterdam University Medical Centre, says, is why research into a vaccine remains a priority: “A vaccine makes you independent from access to drugs.”.

But the US cuts have not only curtailed the preclinical vaccine programme, they have also forced the postponement and scaling back of an HIV vaccine trial in South Africa. They have also affected supporting research, such as surveillance efforts tracking HIV evolution in African countries, says Nairobi-based Vincent Muturi-Kioi, who is leading development of HIV vaccines at the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative in Fresh York City.

Success stories such as the repurposing of lenacapavir as a preventive treatment and progress in vaccine development show the importance of investment in health. It is imperative that HIV vaccine research and deployment continues to receive support, at the same time as rolling out lenacapavir as widely as possible.

It could take more than a decade to translate the encouraging results with germline targeting into an effective HIV vaccine, and the current strategy might encounter more hurdles.

The world is closer than it has ever been to an effective HIV vaccine and has a drug capable of preventing infections. Now is the time for funders to ramp up investment, not cut it back.

Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

📅 25 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish.
  • Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make.
  • Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an key afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

In a recent development, but Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola stated. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

In a recent development, with the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP.

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

Industry observers note that “I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two significant chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an vital moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR.

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite swiftly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

It has been revealed that everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb.

It has been revealed that “The performance was really good,” mentioned Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”.

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix.

It has been revealed that iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu.

Still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

In a recent development, ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very quickly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

There will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

Breaking: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (862 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.
  • "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he remarked on Sunday.
  • But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for new candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.

"Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he remarked on Sunday.

But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for new candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football, people who aren't driven by financial interests," Klopp said ahead of Germany's Nations League match against the Netherlands on Monday.

"If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.".

Sources indicate that if that person is waiting in the wings, they're leaving it late to step on the stage. Despite a raft of federations and continental confederations, including Germany, UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and AFC (Asia), calling for Infantino's head in the wake of his plan to sell off part of the World Cup earlier this year, the incumbent appears to have stopped the bleeding.

That initiative, which involved forming a subsidiary arm of FIFA called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) in order to sell off part of its commercial operations to investors including Joshua Kushner — brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner — was widely panned before being abandoned.

It followed on from widespread criticism of Infantino's awarding of a latest FIFA Peace Prize to Trump, the overturning of a red card for US national team player Folarin Balogun, and with Trump's involvement, at the World Cup and a host of other controversies.

Since then, though, many public critics have backtracked amid FIFA promising to release an extra $2.7bn (€2.45bn) from its reserves over the next four years to the federations, increasing their total investment to $6.35bn.

Perhaps the most significant of these u-turns came from the AFC, who went from saying Infantino had committed a "fundamental breach of trust" in August, to offering the Swiss its "full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a fresh mandate as the FIFA president" in October.

Those words were spoken by AFC President, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who ran against Infantino when he first won the top job at FIFA in 2016. He will not run again and said that "my feeling is, I'm sure, the feeling of most of my members," in regard to Infantino.

Recent findings suggest that proof that the sentiment is not universal comes in the shape of Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA). Tashima is one of only two people to confirm they will oppose Infantino in the March 2027 presidential elections.

The 68-year-old is a well respected figure in Asian football politics and will have no problem meeting the threshold of support from five of FIFA's 211 federations. This is not like the other candidate, former Swiss international player Ramon Vega, who is an enormous outsider. Tashima appears to be running on the basis that he will be able to chart a calmer path at FIFA.

Recent findings suggest that "I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association," Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. "It's not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.".

According to recent reports, but the numbers are against him. Though support from within the confederations may not be total, the backing of AFC and the African confederation (CAF) is a huge boost for Infantino, with those two alone making up 101 votes, almost enough for a majority.

In fact, the only real concern remaining for Infantino remains UEFA. The European federation, headed by Aleksander Ceferin, is a major revenue source for FIFA but the two organizations are at loggerheads. As well as a war of words, UEFA are seeking to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against Infantino in regards to FFE. FIFA have called this a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition".

But, so far, UEFA has not put up a candidate. Former Arsenal coach turned FIFA Chief of Global Football Development, Arsene Wenger was thought to be a contender but has now ruled himself out. Wenger's compatriot, Philippe Diallo, has since emerged as another option, with The Guardian reporting on Monday that the French Football Federation president could be confirmed on Tuesday.

In a recent development, while Europe is football's powerbase, particularly from a club perspective, UEFA will need Diallo, or any candidate they can convince to run, to win votes from outside its 55 nations to have any chance of success, particularly with Tashima likely to split any challenge. Even if a candidate appears before the November 18 deadline, Klopp's hope for change appears to be a long shot.

Martin O’Neill hailed ‘magnificent’ Camilo Duran for helping Celtic win ugly against Torreense to keep their Europa League dream alive.

The Parkhead men looked to be in for a rare comfortable night on the road when Torreense defender Javi Vazquez scored an own goal after nine minutes.

But sloppy defending by the visitors allowed the Portuguese to level 10 minutes later through Dany Jean.

With the minnows sitting in and hoping for a point late on, though, veteran James Forrest climbed off the bench to set up fellow sub Duran for his 15th goal of the season.

On the late impact of the Colombian, O’Neill remarked: ‘I think you always have to keep the faith. But we were gambling almost everything. They were camped outside their penalty area and we were hoping at some stage or another somebody might come up with something.

‘And of course, once again, Duran has done it. He is just a magnificent footballer.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill praised Camilo Duran for once again riding to the rescue.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Fifteen goals and we’re not into December yet. He’s been flying, he’s a terrific player, there’s no question about it.

‘That’s two games he’s come up major for us as well (on back of Besiktas). Maybe 22 games, in all honesty. But he’s been great. He didn’t start the game although we knew he could come on.’.

Although delighted with the result, O’Neill was the first to admit that the performance was not all it might have been.

‘Despite the fact that we’d plenty of possession, I thought that we should just accelerate once or twice, not only just into their half, but also be more penetrative,’ he added.

‘And I think that was the point. I thought we had a lot of ball in the second half as well.

‘There’s always a possibility on the break that you could concede but we had to take the chance because the three points tonight were of vital importance.

‘But, yeah, there’s lots that we can still do to improve our game.’.

Duran's downward header sealed the points for Celtic and ignited their qualification hopes.

The dramatic outcome ensured Celtic are now up to 25th place in the 36-team group – from 32nd – after losing their opening three matches.

O’Neill’s men next face Omonia with Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise to come in January.

Sources indicate that ‘I’m just delighted to have won — it keeps us going,’ added O’Neill. ‘We’ve got six points on the board and we’ve still got a couple of games to go.

‘So, from an absolutely almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we’ve given ourselves some hope.’.

Celtic’s star man on the night, Jota set up the opening goal and relished the return to his homeland almost two years after his last European match.

‘It’s been a long time that I wanted to come back to Portugal and play in front of my friends and family,’ he said. ‘And there’s no better way than with a win with three points. It was something that we wanted to achieve today and luckily we did it.

‘It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible. And right now it’s all about enjoying. There’s no expectation — just to be a professional, having the responsibility of being a Celtic player and delivering every day.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).
  • Recent findings suggest that the goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

Recent findings suggest that the goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is notable because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

"The new negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1.5-degree limit in place," noted Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that the draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1.5C as soon as possible.".

Recognizing a need to address rising carbon emissions, the draft highlighted efforts to "urgently and rapidly" scale up controversial technologies to capture and store CO2 to bring down atmospheric carbon levels.

In a recent development, "For the first time, all the parties here are grappling with the fact that the world will inevitably exceed 1.5 degrees. Negotiators must deliver a response," stated Ani Dasgupta, president of the World Resources Institute, adding that this meant going beyond slashing emissions.

"This requires scaling carbon removal through both nature-based solutions like restoring forests and wetlands, or emerging technologies that directly capture carbon from air," he told reporters.

Kaiser, however, criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry.".

Other activists have dismissed carbon capture as a "false solution" being promoted by corporations.

Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think tank E3G, was cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but remarked it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs.".

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she remarked in a statement.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Representatives of developing nations and small island states, regions bearing the brunt of the climate crisis, have protested climate inaction and a lack of financial support in recent days.

Industry observers note that "Climate finance isn't an extra at these talks: it's the condition for everything else," remarked Rukiya Khamis, program manager for East Africa with environmental group 350.org. "It's alarming how financial pledges by wealthy, polluting countries are dropping like a stone — COP31 must stop this with a strong outcome on adaptation finance.".

"Now we must fight to keep this [adaption finance] in the final decision and ensure these promises become real, grant-based money," remarked Harjeet Singh of the Fill The Fund campaign, which calls on rich countries and corporations to deliver the funding needed for climate-related loss and damage, such as homes destroyed by floods and harvests ruined by drought.

"Communities are suffering devastating losses and damages today precisely because we failed to deliver adaptation at the right time," added Singh.

At 18 pages and 144 items, the draft will be the focus of lengthy discussions in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by Friday. Some observers went so far as to say the document's scope was too wide to be taken seriously.

It has been revealed that "The draft final declaration reads like a Christmas wish list," said Niklas Höhne, a climate policy expert at the NewClimate Institute in Germany. "There are even several points on which we will obviously not be able to reach a consensus, including for example the proposal that developed countries achieve net-zero emissions by 2030.".

But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

It has been revealed that "The general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters Monday. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have said to me that they want to help get an outcome.".

David Waskow, director of WRI's International Climate Initiative, said the draft text demonstrated a level of "seriousness" on important issues like finance, electrification, oceans, overshoot scenarios and emissions of greenhouse gases including methane, which has a warming impact more than 80 times stronger than CO2.

It has been revealed that "The question is whether the level of ambition on those concerns is carried through into the final outcome here," remarked Waskow. "And that's what we need to be watching closely over the coming days.".

Additional reporting by Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.
